a) Reputation for Holiness

The de visu testimonies gathered in the Ordinary Process, and the de auditu and de auditu a videntibus ones drawn from the Supplementary Diocesan Inquiry, as well as the trial and extrajudicial documentation, allow us to address the subject of the Servant of God Sister Anna del Salvatore's reputation for holiness in its real dimensions, both in vita, in morte, and post mortem; and as to the continuity of this reputation down to our own day.

Because of the virtues she practiced in an extraordinary and heroic way, Sister Anna del Salvatore already in vita appears surrounded by a most notable reputation for holiness. Among all who knew her or heard of her, she was esteemed for her immense charity. This reputation spread not only among the poor and those of humble origins but also took root in the hearts of Ecclesiastical Authorities, her Superiors, the Sisters of the Institute, and many persons of noble origin.

From the de visu testimonies of the Ordinary Process of Palermo, one perceives the exceptional reputation for holiness that marked the whole of Sister Anna del Salvatore's life.

The first witness of the Ordinary Process, His Excellency the Most Rev. Msgr. Ignazio Zuccaro, who knew and frequented the Servant of God in the last five years of her life, affirms:

"... in life she enjoyed a reputation for holiness because of her virtues, among those who had known her, whether closely or by reputation"337.

Sister Anna Battistina Bertuzzi, the second witness, who had contact with the Servant of God both in Piacenza and in Palermo, testifies:

"While she lived, Sister Anna del Salvatore enjoyed a reputation as a holy religious, and everyone held her as such: for her virtues, despite her reserve, showed themselves quite clearly and plainly"338.

"I attest and confirm... the opinion held of her as a religious of holy life while she was alive.

... the Servant of God, wherever she went to care for the sick, was admired and venerated as a true angel from Heaven.

... many people, even from the highest aristocracy of Palermo, often came to seek the Servant of God, whether for counsel or to obtain special graces through her prayers, so great was the opinion commonly held of her truly singular virtues339.

... Of the veneration in which the Servant of God was held in all the houses where she served as Superior, I fully attest, this being also known to me. As I also attest to the veneration in which she was held among the laity and the clergy of our city of Palermo340.

... this esteem continued until her death"341.

Sister Anna M. T. Patti di Sorrentino, the fourth witness, recalls:

"The Servant of God's reputation for holiness, even in life, began from the day when, being slandered, ... she bore with heroic resignation what she subsequently had to suffer. This reputation for holiness was maintained not only in the Institute, but also among the people who knew her. I also know that Mother Gattorno held a very high opinion of the Servant of God, to the point of asking her for advice and prayers"342.

Fr. Enrico Filiti343, the Servant of God's confessor and the third witness, testifies:

"I can attest that all the people who knew her retain an opinion of the Servant of God's holiness"344.

Likewise, Fr. Giuseppe Palazzotto, the fifth witness, attests:

"... even while the Servant of God was alive, the opinion of her sanctity was general"345.

Sister Anna Serafina Gregory, the sixth witness, declares:

"... the Sisters of the Institute and everyone else who came close to her considered the Servant of God a Saint"346.

Confirmation of this reputation for holiness is also expressed with particular force by Blessed Rosa Gattorno, who held the Servant of God in deep esteem, consulted her often, and relied on her prayers. Thus she notes in her private jottings, on 7 June 1885, the day of Sister Anna del Salvatore's death:

"Oh blessed soul... She was my comfort. Oh, how richly gifted with divine lights! She had the gift of prophecy: whatever she asked of the Most Holy Mary was granted her; her union with God was a great thing... Oh, how great she was in the sight of God!"347.

"The public opinion held of her, of a holy life, both in life and after death"348.

Echoing her is the newspaper La Sicilia Cattolica, which, on 12 June 1885, in the obituary of the Servant of God, writes among other things:

"The sad news, spread through our city, filled with grief all who had the fortune to know and come close to so rare a woman and so perfect a religious, and to appreciate her extraordinary virtues. She was an Angel! She was a saint! She was a woman of charity! She was a model of virtue! is heard repeated from everyone's lips"349.

Hence it is no surprise that the foundress Anna Rosa Gattorno, in June 1886, asked the Archbishop of Palermo that the Servant of God's remains be placed in a repository, there being great

"the public opinion held of her, of a holy life, both in life and after death"350.

Afterwards, in a writing of 14 February 1887, placed in the coffin on the occasion of the first recognition and the reinterment in a "repository," it is affirmed:

"Sister Anna del Salvatore, journeying from one city of Italy to another, left wherever she passed her blessed footprints imprinted, assisting and consoling human infirmities everywhere, and leaving behind her immense longing and boundless blessing"351.

From the de auditu and de auditu a videntibus testimonies of the Supplementary Ordinary Process as well, and from the very many reports written, mostly in letter form — between 1886 and 1960 — by numerous Sisters, priests, and laypeople, the Servant of God's exceptional reputation for holiness in life is attested.

Sister Anna Margherita Tripi, the first witness of the Supplementary Inquiry, testifies:

"... the Servant of God's reputation for holiness arose even while she was still living... she was called 'the little Saint of Palermo'"352.

Likewise, Sister Anna Elisa Scrò, the second witness of the Supplementary Inquiry, reveals:

"... from my novice mistress I learned that the Servant of God, in Palermo, was esteemed as a holy Sister while she was still alive..."353.

In the report of Sister Anna del Consiglio Chiaramonte we read:

"Although the Servant of God was so modest and reserved in her conduct, attributing to God the merit of working miracles, people nonetheless, edified by such rare modesty, needless to say held her in such high esteem that they called her a saint. People of every class and condition hurried to her for counsel and teaching and to receive heavenly graces and favours. And how many, in the city of Palermo and in other parts of Sicily, experienced the good effects of the miracles worked in life by the Servant of God!"354.

Similarly, in the report of Sister Anna Ulderica Tazzioli, written in the form of a letter to the Superior General Sister Anna Benedetta Carrega, it is shown:

"The dear, holy Superior Salvatore was my Superior in Florence, when Sister A. Giuseppina Tornatore was also there: the two of us were witnesses to very many virtues of that most mortified soul... Blessed is she, who knew so well how to win holy Paradise!"355.

Sister Anna Aniceta Montanari notes:

"Of Sister Anna del Salvatore's reputation for holiness there still echoes an admiration in Palermo: whoever knew her truly loved her as saints are loved and venerated, and still today, when I happen to speak of her with someone who admired her virtues up close, I feel proud to belong to the Family of a sweet saint, as they called her, a saint in feeling and in word"356.

Sister Anna Anastasia Cecconi writes:

"While she lived, most people held her to be a saint; talking with her was a paradise..."357.

Blessed Anna Rosa Gattorno, too, notes in her Memoirs:

"Today was a day of sorrows, and I had only the comfort of my dear Sister Anna del Salvatore, who comforted me in many things, telling me to be calm: Oh, the sight of this dear daughter is such a comfort and help to me! I ask her everything as when she was here below among us wretched ones. She answers me with broken but sure words, or with signs... Oh beautiful soul, steeped in charity! Even now, of this fair gift of yours, you make yourself felt even from Paradise"358.

The opinion of the holiness of the Servant of God Sister Anna del Salvatore, which had ripened in life not only among her Sisters but also among the people who came into contact with her, is confirmed in a particular way on the occasion of her death and in the years that followed, strengthened also by the graces received through her intercession.

When word spread of the serious illness that led to Sister Anna del Salvatore's death, many people from different social classes hurried weeping to her bedside, recalling the many benefits they had received from her, her words, and her exceptional virtues.

The deep sorrow over the Servant of God's death extended also to the Mother General, to the Ecclesiastical Authorities, and to all her Sisters.

On her deathbed, many saw a ray of sunlight reflected on her serene face, which seemed to everyone that of a saint.

To learn what happened at the Servant of God's death, we report above all the de visu testimonies, certainly the most immediate.

His Excellency the Most Rev. Msgr. Ignazio Zuccaro, the first witness, recalls:

"I recall that the Servant of God died in the year 1885, of fever, in the house of the Palazzo Briuccia, top floor, in the room to the right as one enters. The illness lasted only a few days, and in it the Servant of God did not belie her virtue: she received the Holy Sacraments of the Church amid the Community's emotion359.

The body of the Servant of God, as soon as she died, was laid out in the Institute's chapel, if I recall correctly; and on the third day the funeral was held in the same chapel, attended by a very select number of people, not only ordinary citizens but also ladies. On that occasion, the late canon Gaetano Gabriele read a funeral oration, in which he recalled the Servant of God's virtues. Many people asked for relics of her"360.

The already cited Sister Anna Battistina Bertuzzi, the second witness, who was present at the Servant of God's death, relates:

"She received the last sacraments at her own request. She was quite glad to die. Her death was truly precious for the calm and tranquility that accompanied it.... Many people hurried when news of her death spread: persons of standing came to venerate her body, and asked for keepsakes and relics. I myself, before any other, took for myself the veil she wore on her head, and cut off her hair. Everyone said a saint had died, and praised her truly admirable virtues. When the body was later carried to the Cemetery of St. Ursula, many gentlemen sent their carriages in homage to the Servant of God"361.

In the deposition given to the Tribunal of Palermo, Sister Anna Battistina Bertuzzi declares:

"... I too was present at the Servant of God's final illness and was able, together with my other Sisters, to admire the beautiful virtues she showed: patience, resignation, and the cheerfulness with which she bore the torments of the illness afflicting her"362.

"... Of the tributes the public newspapers also paid her in our city, this is well known, and is known to me as well.

... I likewise attest and confirm what is said here about the presence of many people, especially the ladies of Palermo, at those solemn obsequies, and about the fine funeral oration given by the late Fr. Gaetano Gabriele"363.

Further on in her deposition, answering the Postulator's Articles, she affirms:

"Truly, many people, of every condition, flocked to our House to venerate the Servant of God's mortal remains after her death. The Prince of Fitalia and the Princess, his wife, wished, at their own expense, to have the Servant of God's body photographed"364.

Meanwhile, on 15 June 1885, at the end of the memorial celebration for Sister Anna del Salvatore, she had written thus to the Foundress Mother Anna Rosa Gattorno:

"Oh Mother, be content, for that beautiful soul must be of great help; how much she will do before God! Yes, yes, Mother, I feel that she truly has great power, because she loved the Lord too much.

Mother, if only I could speak to you in person, oh how much I would tell you about this... I must tell you, and I repeat, that Salvatore is a saint, and a great saint"365.

Significant is the testimony of Fr. Enrico Filiti, the third witness, who declares:

"As the Servant of God's confessor, I was present at her final illness and her death. She received the last Sacraments with faith and fervour and seemed to long to be joined to her divine Spouse. I recall that she called the Sisters around her bed and exhorted them to observe the Institute's Rule. Among them, many, moved by affection and reverence for the Servant of God, had come from various towns on the island, as though to pay homage to her holiness.

Many people hurried to the Sisters' House chapel to venerate the body laid out there. Among these people were some of high social standing. And all vied with one another to obtain some relic of the Servant of God, especially the Sisters"366.

Sister Anna M. T. Patti di Sorrentino, the fourth witness, relates:

"The Servant of God died on 7 June 1885, of ancylostomiasis fever. I went to visit her every day, and I could observe her tranquility and resignation; indeed, she showed herself glad to die.

... I learned, however, that the body was laid out in the Sisters' Chapel and that many people went to see her"367.

Fr. Giuseppe Palazzotto, the fifth witness, recounts:

"Although I did not visit the Servant of God every day in her final illness, which in any case lasted but a few days, I nonetheless heard it said and was able to confirm that the Servant of God bore her sufferings with resignation and cheerfulness.

When the Servant of God's death occurred, many people of every condition went to visit the body laid out in the Sisters' inner chapel, at the Briuccia house. All vied with one another to obtain some relic. The same happened when she was buried at the Cemetery of St. Ursula. All this I attest, having been present in those places"368.

Sister Anna Serafina Gregory, the sixth witness, asserts:

"... I can attest that, having gone with Sister Anna Teresa Patti to visit the Servant of God on her deathbed, we found her suffering greatly, but cheerful and glad to die, longing to be united with the Lord"369.

The obituary of the Servant of God published by the newspaper La Sicilia Cattolica on 12 June 1885, and the funeral eulogy delivered by Fr. Gaetano Gabriele, canon of the Metropolitan Cathedral of Palermo, later printed, indicate the resonance that Sister Anna del Salvatore's death had throughout the whole Institute of the Daughters of St. Anne and among the population, especially of Palermo370.

His Excellency, then Canon, Msgr. Ignazio Zuccaro, deeply grieved at the loss of the Servant of God, wrote thus to the Foundress Mother Anna Rosa Gattorno:

"It is truly like a dream, the loss of Sister Anna Salvatore. I can tell you that the whole city is deeply grieved by it, and even my own Eminence showed himself profoundly moved, and was touched when, on returning to the Palace, I found him already informed of the sorrowful event.

All the Sisters are inconsolable, but we have sought to avoid excessive displays, exhorting them to resignation, and they have conducted themselves wisely.

Even less devout people recognise that the loss has been irreparable, and they are right, for one does not often find so many graces in a creature, further nourished by so much correspondence with grace.

... She remained fully present to herself until the last moment, and died as she had lived, as a true saint"371.

Likewise, the Princess of Fitalia, Emilia Laberiska Settimo, who held the Servant of God in great esteem, communicates in a letter to the Mother the preparations for the solemn funeral:

"The preparations for the funeral have begun, and it is hoped the ceremony will turn out beautiful and solemn. Many people have contributed to this end, and I believe the expenses will be covered by the offering born of the gratitude and admiration of all who had the fortune to know this blessed soul."

And she adds:

"Ah! My Mother, what a terrible emptiness we feel... I have gone twice to the Briuccia House; the emptiness is terrible, but it is also a great consolation to see again these walls, witnesses of such holiness and heroic virtue"372.

We also read in the report of Sister Anna Paolina Viani:

"It is impossible to describe our grief at such a loss; we were inconsolable; the thought of never again seeing on this earth our Beloved Superior, who had given us so many sublime examples of holiness, was heart-rending; our only comfort was knowing her in Heaven, enjoying the Highest Good, the reward of her heroic virtues; we had recourse to her intercession and prayed that from above she would protect us and pray for us.

Not only we, but the whole citizenry of Palermo was moved and wept at her passing, and proclaimed her a saint, and had recourse, and still have recourse, to her intercession in their needs"373.

Mrs. Ines Zecca, the eleventh witness of the Supplementary Inquiry, declares:

"I have heard it said that, in Palermo, when she died, many people of different backgrounds were present and considered her a person worthy of veneration, because she had done so much good, especially to the needy, and they said a saint had died"374.

In the Ordinary Process of Palermo, conducted between 1896 and 1907, some de visu witnesses testify about the great veneration that took hold in the years following Sister Anna del Salvatore's death.

Sister Anna Battistina Bertuzzi, the second witness, attests:

"In our Institute there is much devotion to the Servant of God, and people always and frequently go to her tomb to venerate her and to pray in order to obtain some special grace.

This reputation for holiness of the Servant of God has not diminished after her death; on the contrary, it has spread and become widespread not only here in Palermo and in our Houses of Sicily, but also abroad; for in the Mother House this devotion to the Servant of God is very widespread"375.

"The Servant of God died on 7 June 1885. About two years after her death, at the request of many prominent people, Cardinal Celesia granted that the Servant of God's body be placed in a repository. The Mother General then came to Palermo expressly to attend that ceremony. Indeed, in the presence of Msgr. Cirino, then Vicar General of the Archdiocese, and of the whole staff of the Curia, of our Mother General, and of many distinguished figures, both ecclesiastical and lay, the Servant of God's body was exhumed and placed in a repository.

I attest that the devotion aroused at that moment, when the coffin was opened, was real, and how all those present vied with one another, some to touch the body, others to obtain some object of the Servant of God's.

... This eagerness to have relics and news of the Servant of God is known to me as well. And this on account of the Servant of God's beautiful virtues"376.

Fr. Giuseppe Palazzotto, the fifth witness, confirms:

"Even after her death the opinion of the Servant of God's holiness continued, and the expression is widespread: 'We shall doubtless see her upon the Altars'"377.

"When the Servant of God's death occurred, people came asking me for photographs of the Servant of God, which I had made and hastened to send to all who asked for them, in great numbers.

... the Servant of God is invoked by her devotees"378.

Sister Anna Serafina Gregory, the sixth witness, declares:

"This reputation for holiness of the Servant of God grew even after her death; and I know that many commended themselves to her intercession, and still today hold much devotion and trust in her: the late Foundress Mother too nourished this devotion and trust. Indeed she commended herself to her often, particularly in certain most serious circumstances. And it was she who wished that the Cause of Beatification of the Servant of God be promoted"379.

The long interruption of the Ordinary Process, as we explained in the section on the Evidence, did not, however, interrupt the continuation of the reputation for holiness enjoyed by the Servant of God.

A significant proof of this can be found in the three recognitions of the Servant of God's body that took place in 1887, 1932, and 1957380, aimed at providing a better arrangement for the tomb and making it easier for people to have access to the Servant of God. Nor can it be said that the change of tomb would have deterred the flow of people, as the Episcopal Chancellor rightly observed, stating he was certain that the devotion of those who loved the Servant of God would not be turned away by the change of burial place381.

The Historical Experts write in their report regarding the continuity of the reputation for holiness:

"Sister Anna del Salvatore's reputation for holiness has not been extinguished by her death; on the contrary, it has become ever more firmly established. There emerges from the documents the interest in her life, the veneration aroused by the various recognitions of her mortal remains, the memory that remains of her in her native town of Albareto, where the nursery school bears her name.

In the Institute of the Daughters of St. Anne the echo of her virtues and the expectation that her holiness would be recognised has never died out, and this led to the request of the 1984 Chapter Assembly to resume the Cause of Beatification of Sister Anna del Salvatore"382.

In the Supplementary Diocesan Inquiry of Palermo, conducted between 1995 and 2000, the witnesses were unanimous in testifying to the continuing reputation for holiness of Sister Anna del Salvatore, still very much alive today in people's hearts. We therefore think it useful to report a few excerpts from their statements.

Sister Anna Elisa Scrò, the second witness of the Supplementary Inquiry, testifies:

"... after her death, her reputation for holiness spread among the faithful, who called her 'the little Saint of Palermo.'

I entered the religious Institute of the Daughters of St. Anne in 1930 and, from then until today, in the various houses of ours where I have lived, the figure of Sister Anna del Salvatore has always been esteemed and venerated as a saint"383.

"During my time in Palermo I was able to confirm that the Servant of God's tomb was frequently visited by the faithful for devotional purposes, and people would sign their names on the tombstone.

I myself went several times to visit that tomb out of devotion, and signed my name there too"384.

Sister Anna Teresina Lo Bue, the third witness of the Supplementary Inquiry, relates:

"The Servant of God was buried in an earthen grave, in the cemetery of 'St. Ursula' in Palermo.

I remember this grave well because I went to visit it many times and always saw it full of flowers, which the faithful who went to visit it certainly placed there.

I learned, in fact, that many devotees went to that grave to implore the Servant of God's intercession, in order to obtain graces from the Lord"385.

Sister Anna Silvina Margiotta, the fifth witness of the Supplementary Inquiry, attests:

"As for her reputation for holiness, I can only say that it has been spreading not only in our Communities but also among the faithful, particularly since it was decided to resume her Cause for beatification"386.

"I have gone several times to visit the Servant of God's first grave, and now, every week, I go to the new tomb, both to clean the chapel and out of particular devotion. I can attest that the Servant of God's two tombs have been and are places that draw many of the faithful, who showed and still show their devotion by placing flowers and stopping to pray. Weekly I am nearly obliged to bring holy cards of the Servant of God, prepared by the Postulation, in order to satisfy the faithful's continual requests"387.

Mrs. Maria Tomaselli, the thirteenth witness of the Supplementary Inquiry, from Albareto, the Servant of God's native town, recounts:

"This is what an aunt of mine used to tell me, pointing out to me the house in Albareto where Sister Anna del Salvatore was born and raised: 'Here a saint was born!' Moreover, that same aunt regarded the room where the Sister was born almost as a chapel. In the parish, prayers are often said for her beatification"388.

Mrs. Bice Borella, the fifteenth witness of the Supplementary Inquiry, also from Albareto, affirms:

"We too, from childhood, used to pray and remember Sister Anna del Salvatore because 'she was truly good' — we were told — 'more than an ordinary sister!' I hold her in devotion, and, though with alternating phases, I continue to pray to her. In years past, around 1950–1954, I remember some people carried off, 'as a kind of relic,' little pieces of the wooden floor of the room where the Servant of God had been born"389.

Fr. Paolo Tomaselli, the eighteenth witness of the Supplementary Inquiry, parish priest for many years in the Servant of God's home parish, himself a convinced advocate of her holiness, says among other things in his deposition:

"I possess a small piece of cloth that belonged to the Servant of God, given to me by a woman on her deathbed. Since 1992, a particular 'devotion' to the Servant of God has begun in my parish community, and we recite the prayer for her beatification every day. In particular, we celebrate the anniversary of her birth (the first Sunday of February), often with the presence of the Bishop or the Vicar General"390.

And Fr. Duilio Odoidio Schiavetta, parish priest of S. Quirico di Albareto, the twentieth witness of the Supplementary Inquiry, confirms:

"The reputation for holiness, in the faithful's opinion, has certainly always existed since she died, perhaps even while she was still alive, and this reputation remained alive for a long time. Recently, and specifically since 1992, on the 150th anniversary of her birth, popular interest in the Servant of God has increased again. On that occasion the Vicar General of the Diocese of Pontremoli-Massa was also present at the celebrations"391.

Sister Vincenzina Scalzo, the sixteenth witness of the Supplementary Inquiry, reaffirms:

"When I came to Albareto, where I carry out my mission, I always heard talk of Sister Anna del Salvatore, both from the elderly and from the former parish priest. People said she was truly a saint"392.

"When the parish priest Don Duilio printed a little booklet on the Servant of God's life, people immediately took it up and constantly ask for her holy cards, expressing great devotion"393.

Sister Roberta Cecilia Frati, Daughter of St. Anne, concluding her biographical profile published in 1995, writes:

"The fame of Sister Anna del Salvatore's charity and virtues has crossed the borders of Palermo and Sicily, and has withstood the passage of time, reaching us more than a century after her death"394.

Indeed, the Servant of God's reputation for holiness, as we have tried to show, has always remained alive over time and has spread ever more down to our own day, strengthened also by the many and continual graces attributed to her intercession.

b) Reputation for Signs

In confirmation of the reputation for holiness that has always surrounded, through the years, and still today surrounds the memory of the Servant of God, we can affirm that the graces attributed to her intercession are numerous.

Even the witnesses of the Ordinary Process of Palermo report graces received through Sister Anna del Salvatore's intercession.

Sister Anna Battistina Bertuzzi, the second witness, relates precisely an extraordinary grace that concerns her own person:

"... Traveling from Caltanissetta to Terranova by carriage with other Sisters, at a certain point the horses took fright. It was a moment of great fear. I jumped from the back of the carriage and pulled the Sisters with me. At that moment I felt nothing; but the next day I began to feel pains. I had to set off again, but just as I was about to get into the carriage, I felt such pains that I could not bear it. A hernia had formed, because of the jump I had made, which tormented me horribly. During the night I felt I was dying. The doctor had said that the next day I would, without fail, have to undergo surgery. He said: either surgery or death. But I turned to our Sister Anna Salvatore, asking her to obtain for me a little relief from my terrible pains. I applied the Servant of God's photograph and veil to my stomach. At a certain moment I felt, in the affected area, something like a knot coming undone. I lay down and the pains ceased, and I immediately felt cured. I called the Sisters to rejoice with me, so that I was able to continue my journey. The next day, when the doctors came, they marveled at my recovery and did not know to what to attribute it, except to a miracle... 'I have obtained special graces from the Servant of God in the exercise of my office as Provincial of this Province of Sicily, and not only that, but also personal ones, both in the moral and the material order'"395.

Sister Anna M. T. Patti di Sorrentino, the fourth witness, reports:

"... I add a wondrous event that happened to Sister Teresa Macaluso, Superior and foundress of the Institute of the Sacred Hearts in Palermo. She had a sarcoma on her neck, which the doctors judged absolutely incurable and which could not be operated on at all. Meanwhile, the good Sister Macaluso effectively commended herself to the Servant of God, applying to herself an object that had belonged to her. What happened was that, a few days later, the sarcoma disappeared completely. This event astonished those close to her, such as Cavaliere Lanolina, my sister the Princess of Torrebuona, and others, and also the very doctor, Cataliotti, who had treated her and declared her incurable. He was so amazed at the fact that, going down the stairs, he kept exclaiming: 'A miracle, a miracle'"396.

In the Supplementary Diocesan Process of Palermo, the testimonies of the de auditu and de auditu a videntibus witnesses reaffirm that the Servant of God is prayed to and invoked by numerous devotees. To her intercession are in fact attributed many graces and favours, concerning especially notable healings from serious illnesses.

Sister Anna Margherita Tripi, the first witness of the Supplementary Inquiry, points out:

"From a friend of mine, Maria Terranova, I learned that she obtained the following grace through the Servant of God's intercession.

... she was to undergo surgery, as a result of X-ray findings; but when everything was ready for that operation, the doctors noticed that the condition shown by the X-rays had by then disappeared, and therefore did not consider the operation necessary"397.

Mr. Carlo Tozzi, the ninth witness of the Supplementary Inquiry, likewise reports a grace received by his daughter:

"I have had devotion to the Servant of God since 1978, when my daughter Patrizia, born in 1958, was hit by a moped and suffered a torn right posterior cruciate ligament. After surgery, she did not regain mobility in the leg, which remained immobilised for six months. Later, because of a sprain, she was hospitalised again. The situation was serious also because my daughter Patrizia was nursing her five-month-old baby. I prayed with great faith and trust to the Servant of God Sister Anna del Salvatore Orsi that the operation might be avoided, and so it happened: she was discharged the next day. Since then I always carry the Servant of God's image with me and cultivate a certain devotion to her, entrusting myself to her intercession"398.

Likewise, Mrs. Ines Zecca, the eleventh witness of the Supplementary Inquiry, relates the spiritual grace obtained through the Servant of God's intercession, that of her son's conversion:

"On the occasion, however, of the very serious misfortune that befell my son while he was in the military (caught up in the Moon sect), I prayed, together with my husband and my family, to all the saints, and also to Sister Anna del Salvatore, asking for the grace of my son's conversion. And with joy — after four long years — I saw my son return"399.

Similarly, the already cited parish priest of S. Quirico di Albareto, Fr. Duilio Odoidio Schiavetta, the twentieth witness of the Supplementary Inquiry, affirms:

"As for the graces obtained through Sister Anna del Salvatore's intercession, I can report a testimony, dating back to the late 1930s or early 1940s, of a woman in labour and in danger of death who, having invoked the Servant of God together with those present, and placed a relic (a handkerchief) on her belly, was able to give birth safely"400.

Mrs. Rosalia Argento, the twenty-third witness of the Supplementary Inquiry, declares:

"I believe there was her intercession in regard to my own person as well. Indeed, when in 1993 I was hospitalised in Palermo, I was very ill because of a stricture over a 20 cm stretch, I was reduced to 40 kilograms, and I had severe anemia, to the point that I could no longer eat anything at all. I received several transfusions in order to be operated on, and after the operation considerable complications set in. It was at this moment that... I turned, trusting, to Sister Anna del Salvatore. Now I am completely cured and I believe this is owed to the Servant of God's prayers"401.

Mrs. Grazia Ventimiglia, testifying in 1998 in the Supplementary Inquiry as the twenty-fourth witness, recounts the help she received through the Servant of God's intercession in the various surgical operations she underwent in the years from 1959 to 1969. A sister gave her an image of Sister Anna del Salvatore and invited her to turn with faith to her intercession, confident that she would help her. That is just what happened, and the woman says that after the operation her first thought was to thank Sister Anna del Salvatore402.

Under Letter E of the Summarium Documentorum: in Section I, b) Written reports, many accounts are given of graces received through the Servant of God's intercession, some of them described in detail by de visu witnesses and sent in the form of a letter to the Foundress Mother Blessed Rosa Gattorno403; in c) Documents submitted by the Witness-Co-deponent XXVI, five reports are given, handed in by Sister Anna Margherita Saggiomo to the Tribunal, concerning cures obtained in the years 1960–1997, again through Sister Anna del Salvatore's intercession404.

Abundant documentation of the Fama Signorum is given, likewise under Letter E, in Section II, a) Report of Graces received. We have documents and reports of graces obtained through the Servant of God's intercession, mostly cures and particular acts of help that develop, more fully, the mentions of graces already contained in the trial "Reports" made on Sister Anna del Salvatore's life and virtues405.

In the report of Sister Anna Costanza Cenni, sent to the Foundress Blessed Anna Rosa Gattorno, we read:

"Sister A. Battista Cosmano, a novice of the Daughters of St. Anne, fell ill from the very first days of her Taking of the Habit, with a great pain in the belly caused by constipation; she suffered continuous torments. She took a first, a second purgative; a third, which had little effect. Examined by the doctor, he too prescribed her another purge and enemas; but, like the first ones, these only served to calm her for a moment. The pain kept increasing more and more; and it became necessary to resort to an enteroclysm. Forced to take a fourth medicine, this proved even more useless than the others. At the second visit the doctor paid her, he gave her a certain purgative water which, instead, only served to make her feel even more the pains she was suffering, and a constipation that produced a great swelling of the stomach, so that she could neither stand, nor walk, nor sit, nor even eat. Only, out of obedience, did she swallow a few spoonfuls of broth.

More than a month had passed, and the Reverend Superior, seeing that every treatment had become useless, very sorrowfully had to tell her that, since all remedies had become ineffective, the long illness did not allow the Novice to remain in Religious life any longer, finding herself incapable of all that the Rules prescribe, and therefore outside regular observance; the best course, if the Mother General thought so, would be to send her back home. But the Superior was grieved by this and still waited before deciding.

Poor Sister A. Battista could not come to terms with this news; she wept night and day at the thought that, more than the illness itself, the worst evil was having to leave the Institute, and forever. The poor thing wept and did not know where to turn for help, when a Sister (Sister A. Maffea) suggested that she turn in prayer to the late Sister Anna del Salvatore. Encouraged further by her Reverend Novice Mistress, the novice began a novena; and on the very evening of the first day of that novena she had a bowel movement without taking any purgative and felt a quite noticeable improvement, though not free from the usual pains in the belly and the swelling. That same night, after so many sleepless nights, she slept and dreamed...

In the dream she saw three nuns she knew, and one of them asked her why she was weeping. 'I want to see Sister A. del Salvatore, to ask her for a grace (these are her own words).' Sister A. del Salvatore indeed came towards her and asked me why I was so distressed and weeping. I knelt down on seeing her, and told her of the illness I suffered, and that, more than the illness, it was the extreme pain of having to leave Religious life. No, she answered me, the Holy Mother does not wish it; and, touching and pressing my stomach: You have nothing, she added. Be obedient, and having said this, she vanished. I went on sleeping and woke at the sound of the short prayer, together with the other sisters. I got out of bed completely well; and from that day on I have had no more cause for complaint (so the Novice continues). I am very well; I eat with appetite whatever the Community gives me.

... Moreover, the cook Sister A. of the Wounds developed an ailment in one eye; after I myself had cared for her, seeing that it showed no sign of improvement, I had the doctor examine her, who said it was no small matter and that it would not be difficult to lose the eye; indeed, I took her off kitchen duty and had her given every care that human skill knew and could provide, but all in vain. Finally, tired of always seeing her bandaged and using so many remedies, I had every treatment stopped and marked her eye with the photograph of Sister A. Salvatore. This was in the evening; the next day she was already much improved, and after two days I was able to put her back in the kitchen, perfectly cured..."406.

Canon Gaetano Pagliani relates:

"... In the month of October 1888, in a city of Sicily, while I was giving a course of Holy Preaching, a woman approached me, asking for comfort, torn apart by an illness that seriously threatened her health. Grieved by that heart-rending account, I knew of nothing better to suggest than to begin a novena of prayers to the Blessed Memory of Sister Anna del Salvatore Orsi, first purifying herself in Holy Confession and approaching the Most Holy Sacrament of the Eucharist. She answered that she would gladly do so, and that for a year she had not once missed Holy Communion.

Well then, once that novena began, it proved impossible for that woman to approach Holy Communion, so many and so great were the obstacles that opposed her every morning. On the last day of the novena, she came to me dissolved in tears of penance, and revealed to me that she had seen in a dream a little nun, who announced herself by the name of Sister Anna del Salvatore, and who commanded her to open her heart at once in Holy Confession and to convert, lest she suffer terrible scourges.

Repentant and moved, (granting me leave to issue the present statement for the glory of that blessed soul), she revealed to me in confession:

1. that for a full seven years she had belonged to the Masonic sect,

2. that she had abjured the Holy Catholic Religion,

3. that she received Holy Communion in order to offer insult to the Most Holy Body of Jesus Christ,

4. that she had the mission of corrupting young girls, and especially the Sisters of a Religious Community.

She handed over to me the shameful documents of her oaths, the insignia of Freemasonry, and, her soul washed clean in a general Holy Confession, she set out again on the path of truth and salvation..."407.

In the documents submitted by the sole co-deponent witness (twenty-sixth and second ex officio), Sister Anna Margherita Saggiomo, there were reported — as already stated — five accounts concerning cures obtained in the years 1960–1997, again through Sister Anna del Salvatore's intercession. We report some of them below:

"... It is my duty to tell you that my dear only child, 14 months old, was gravely ill from poisoning. The attending doctor told me the baby was very serious, and on 8 September, around 8:30 in the evening, my little one was to fly up to heaven. One cannot imagine the weeping there was in my house. But as soon as the doctor told me the baby was very serious, I turned to the Daughters of St. Anne sisters to pray, and the good sisters gave me a holy card of the Servant of God Sister Anna del Salvatore Orsi, and I put it right beside the baby. The next day, the poisoning had vanished..."408.

"I thank the Servant of God Sister Anna del Salvatore Orsi, who granted me the grace I asked of her, for the healing of my daughter Patrizia's leg.

After an accident, it had remained stiff, but all the tests, including the CT scan, showed nothing. The Servant of God Sister Anna del Salvatore Orsi healed her..."409.

From the writings of the Foundress herself, Blessed Anna Rosa Gattorno, one can likewise see how greatly she relied on the effective intercession of her "dear Sister Anna del Salvatore," so that she constantly turned to her in her prayers to obtain many graces for herself, for the Sisters, for the Institute:

"Oh, what a night! I could not close my eyes anymore; I felt myself growing faint with weariness, and I prayed for a grace that so occupied my mind, for a poor Daughter of St. Anne who was suffering so much: I asked my Sister Anna del Salvatore, and she answered me: — It is all over, she is well, it is nothing. — But how? The doctors say it takes far too long to heal! — Not at all, it is all over:

Today she writes to me that it is all over and that she is cured. Oh, for me it was a true miracle, a very great grace that dear Sister Anna del Salvatore obtained from God!... Oh, truly, more and more I come to know what a beautiful soul she is, and whatever she asks, she obtains from Jesus! She can refuse Him nothing for her Institute, it is plain to see"410.

The religious name of our Servant of God already contains in itself, and at the same time ideally represents, her constitutive spiritual character, for she wished to be spiritually bound to the Saviour, to Jesus the Redeemer, in a mission of help to those in need in body and spirit.

All her work of ascetic perfection was anchored in the unshakable foundation of the commitment to love God above all things and to strive for holiness also through heroic service to the suffering neighbour, as is found in the charism of the Institute of the Daughters of St. Anne.

The second Theological Censor of the Servant of God's writings writes thus in his vote:

"[The Servant of God's letters], although they do not provide many elements that directly reveal the Servant of God's inner life, allow us to sketch her spiritual physiognomy with sufficient certainty.

In the rigorous and scrupulous communication to the Foundress or to the Sisters regarding the state of the communities and their work, the features of her personality lie hidden. Through constancy in the practice of virtue and in fulfilling the duties of her state with the responsibilities entrusted to her, the Servant of God shows to what degree she had assimilated the spirit of the Institute, in the meticulous observance of the Rule and in unconditional obedience to the Foundress and to her direct superiors. The testimony of her diligence in living out that spirit, especially in caring for the sick and in fidelity to the Rule, down to a few days before her death, even while already gravely ill, shows the heroic endurance of this woman, who tirelessly strives to obey and thereby to follow the divine will"411.

In the Supplementary Diocesan Inquiry of Palermo, some de auditu a videntibus witnesses grasp exhaustively the characteristic traits of Sister Anna del Salvatore.

Sister Anna Margherita Tripi, the first witness of the Supplementary Inquiry, observes:

"It seems to me that the characteristic note of the Servant of God's spirituality is to be found in her generous charity towards the poor. And in this respect, she could be a model for contemporary society"412.

Sister Anna Teresina Lo Bue, the third witness of the Supplementary Inquiry, declares:

"... the virtue that stands out most in her life is humility"413.

"... besides the Servant of God's great humility, I can add that characteristic notes of her spirituality were charity towards the poor and her spirit of penance and prayer..."414.

Sister Anna Gaetanina Zupone, the seventh witness of the Supplementary Inquiry, reveals:

"The Servant of God was marked by great humility and a spirit of sacrifice, both in the community where she lived and towards the poorest; wherever she passed she always brought a touch of peace, of serenity. She always stood out for her motherly spirit, for obedience, poverty, and simplicity, virtues all lived in a heroic way"415.

"... the characteristic notes of the Servant of God's spirituality are poverty of heart and motherly self-giving"416.

Fr. Duilio Odoidio Schiavetta, the twentieth witness of the Supplementary Inquiry, attests:

"The ordinary life lived in a heroic way, I believe, is the characteristic of Sister Anna del Salvatore, her readiness towards her Sisters and her total obedience to her superiors, even in conditions of precarious health. And, further, the spirit of sacrifice exercised heroically.

As for her spirituality, I think she had a total abandonment to God even when, at a certain point in her life, she was heavily slandered, accepting all this as God's permission"417.

We believe, however, that the most beautiful and explicit testimony of Anna del Salvatore's spirituality is offered to us by Blessed Anna Rosa Gattorno, at the moment of her request to the Archbishop of Palermo for the grant of a "repository" for the Servant of God's burial. Praising the spirituality the Servant of God had lived, confirmed also in death and after death, she expressed herself thus:

"The heroic virtues practiced by the Servant of God within and outside the religious house, accompanied by a humility at once simple and profound, with an impenetrable spirit of self-concealment.

The spirit of prayer and union with God, which raised her to the highest contemplation.

The spirit of the harshest penance, with which she sacrificed herself to her God.

The ready and tireless charity in caring for the sick of every kind.

The kindness towards her fellow Sisters, for whom she always had motherly tenderness.

The odour of sanctity that accompanied her death, with unmistakable signs of predestination and salvation.

The public opinion held of her, of a holy life, both in life and after death"418.

The first Theological Censor writes:

"[From reading the letters] There clearly appear the total self-giving to the point of exhausting her physical strength, and a heroic submission of her own reasons and feelings for the sake of the mission progressively entrusted to her. Yet there is always present a surprising sense of evangelical optimism, which can be abundantly observed in the constancy of her human attitude in the face of various circumstances, even the most difficult ones; in her conviction of the perfectibility of plans; in the expectations placed in other people; in the good humour that often breaks through in some of her expressions of wonder"419.

In the report of the Historical Experts we read:

"Sister Anna del Salvatore was a shining example of faithful following of the Lord and of generous, boundless charity towards her brothers and sisters, because in her life she entrusted herself totally to the Lord, letting herself be guided and shaped by him, growing continually in the knowledge of Jesus and in his love, and continually widening her capacity for concrete and effective self-giving"420.

We can also come to know the heights reached by the Servant of God's spirituality through the account of her last hours of life, described by Sister Anna Battistina Bertuzzi in two letters to the Foundress Mother:

"'So I placed myself at her right side and did not leave her until her last breath, and those 3 hours in which I attended her were a true consolation because of her joy, which she showed both in words and with smiles. So every minute she took up her Crucifix and, clasping it, kissed it; the Confessor, who never left her, would say to her from time to time: Salvatore, remember Jesus and Mary. Yes, Father. And then always her word Fiat'; ..." "Oh Mother, be content, for that beautiful soul must be of great help; how much she will do before God! Yes, yes, Mother, I feel that she truly has great power, because she loved the Lord too much"421.

In the biography of Blessed Anna Rosa Gattorno, where the Servant of God's death is discussed, we read the following:

"She was a jewel of the Institute, so lofty was her spirituality, her genuine kindness towards her fellow Sisters, and her deep humility. Wholly given over to the service of God, Sister Anna del Salvatore also had a very special love for religious poverty and sought to live it radically... poor among the poor. For the poor she made herself a beggar, as she did for her fellow Sisters too"422.

Holiness is, for Sister Anna del Salvatore, the only goal worth pursuing. She wants to be herself a holy Sister, but she also wants her fellow Sisters to be holy, as well as all the sick and the people she drew near to and served.

One of the means to reach holiness was the richness of her humanity, nourished and strengthened by a spirit of faith that made her see, in her neighbour — especially the sick and needy — Jesus, who continues to suffer and to redeem the world. The acts of charity performed by the Servant of God are innumerable and of the most varied kinds; carried out towards every class and category of person, with an exact understanding of situations, characters, and the dispositions of the moment. Sister Anna del Salvatore had the art of making happy those who lived close to her, giving them confidence, security, and peace. Near her, one did not feel fear, but rather sensed that there was someone who was like God's goodness, made sensitive to one's own frailty in order to help it. Of the souls entrusted to her, whether her fellow Sisters or the sick, she knew everything, and gave to each what was fitting: the word of comfort or the warning, the exhortation and the encouragement, physical or material help, and spiritual help.

It should be added that Sister Anna del Salvatore's charity knew no exceptions or restrictions of any kind. With those who loved her she was kind, and with those who, without meaning to, caused her pain, she was even kinder and more charitable.

In Sister Anna del Salvatore we have the perfect testimony of a most profound spirit of faith, of a boundless charity, which never has anything to forgive but everything to be forgiven for; of a humility nourished in the everyday.

In the life of the Church, consecrated souls who enriched and perfumed it with the heroism of their virtues have never been lacking. In these exemplary figures, much more than in the past, we today feel drawn by the holiness that shows itself in the daily and constant practice of an exemplary life, in a dedication to the Lord that knows no paths so steep as to discourage more than to stir emulation.

These chosen souls are our models and teachers of life, and it comforts us to see them fighting the same battles as we do, and labouring to reach the victorious goals to which we too aspire.

One of these generous souls, great in the simplicity of an unfailing attachment to duty, is precisely Sister Anna del Salvatore.

Her life flows along plain and tranquil in the eyes of her fellow Sisters, who still today admire her sublime goodness and charity, her constant dedication, her continual effort to arrive at offering herself totally to Jesus. Her Christian commitment to the sick, the poor, and the needy is still today an example and a stimulus for everyone.

Thus testifies Sister Anna Gaetanina Zupone, the seventh witness of the Supplementary Inquiry:

"The Servant of God, in my opinion, in today's historical moment can give a great impetus to being a model for us, Daughters of St. Anne, and for all who are committed, in the Church, to going out to the poor and, in a particular way, to those who suffer"423.

The same witness adds:

"I believe that the Servant of God can point out to today's world the Father's merciful love"424.

In confirmation of what has been said, we report other testimonies gathered in the Supplementary Diocesan Inquiry, conducted between 1995 and 2000, in the Archiepiscopal Curia of Palermo.

Mr. Pietro Spanò, the twenty-first witness of the Supplementary Inquiry, who considers himself to have received a "miracle" from the Servant of God and who, in her life, singles out above all her dedication to others, particularly to those who suffer, states precisely:

"I believe that the message the Servant of God conveys to today's society is the experience of closeness, solidarity, sharing, and participation in the world of suffering."425

Fr. Giuseppe Conti, the twenty-fifth witness (first ex officio) of the Supplementary Inquiry, a priest and parish pastor, reaffirms:

"I think that today the Servant of God can give everyone an effective message of evangelical life, which I hope for especially for all the sisters and for us priests"426.

Sister Anna Margherita Saggiomo, too, the sole co-deponent witness (twenty-sixth and second ex officio) of the Supplementary Inquiry, considers that the Servant of God can be pointed to as a model of Christian life, and affirms:

"I believe that Sister Anna del Salvatore, in this complex time of ours in which having dominates, can be a valid model of life, showing everyone the path of holiness in daily life, living in evangelical simplicity, in dedication, and in knowing how to give value to suffering"427.

To conclude our reflection on the message Sister Anna del Salvatore leaves us today, we report what Sister Anna Roberta Cecilia Frati writes in the Servant of God's biographical profile, of 1995:

"Her simplicity, the truthfulness of her life, her unsparing giving of herself for those who suffer constitute a strong call back to the Gospel and lead us to reflect on what is truly essential in life, because we shall be judged on charity: 'Whatever you did for the least of these brothers and sisters of mine, you did for me' (Mt 25:40)"428.

By putting God's saving Word into practice in her life, Sister Anna del Salvatore indeed bore exemplary witness to the essence of the Gospel message: the "new commandment of love" (Jn 13:34).

Illumined by the love of God, Sister Anna del Salvatore had drawn precisely from that love the fortitude of spirit that sustained her on her path as a religious, undertaken with absolute resolve.

From the moment of her sincere response to God's call, she never gave up her commitment to carrying out the plan of holiness, loving to the end (Jn 13:1).

Worshiping God the Father in spirit and truth, she followed Christ in order to merit a share in His glory.

In her life, therefore, the mark of the Kingdom of God was made manifest. Reserving for herself nothing of what made up her daily offering, the Servant of God directed all her actions to the Father and effectively bore witness, through Faith, to the value of the goods to come.

By presenting her figure, the intent is in fact to raise awareness in other people, young people in particular, so that they may be spurred to give meaning to their own lives; to recover the perennial values of Christian asceticism; to learn that time and energy are given to us to glorify God and neighbour; to rediscover the taste for belonging totally to God.

Sister Anna del Salvatore is one of the witnesses of every age in whom God has clearly shown men His motherly and merciful presence; and she is a small light for all who agree to follow the Lord with a strong and generous self-giving.

Most Eminent Cardinals, Most Excellent Bishops,

Most Reverend Consultors,

In this third millennium, when humanity looks towards a future laden with unknowns, it seems to us most useful to reflect on people who, under the Spirit's action, embodied in a simple yet profound and consistent way the Gospel message of love, in humble and passionate service to Christ, to the Church, to society.

Even though she lived more than a century ago, Sister Anna del Salvatore can well be called a woman of our time, who, in the profession of the evangelical counsels, committed her whole self to the true progress of the human person.

The presentation of her figure to the People of God thus constitutes a truly singular sign, which points to Jesus and reminds modern man, too often distracted by comfort and technological achievements, of the need to break free of his own selfishness in order to rediscover the roots of truth and life, that is, the mystery of love sanctified by the sacrifice of Jesus, which brings forth salvation.

In entrusting, therefore, the present work to your authoritative and careful study, as well as to the possible examination of the Historical Consultors, we hope that it will not only be favourably received, but that it will be possible to arrive at a positive, well-grounded judgment on the heroicity of the Servant of God's virtues. This is the wish and, at the same time, the petition put forward with intimate and confident expectation by: the Postulator and the Congregation of the Daughters of St. Anne, worthy custodian of Sister Anna del Salvatore's spiritual heritage; all the members of the other Branches joined to the same religious Family; as well as the Bishops and the numerous faithful, particularly of the Dioceses of Palermo, Pontremoli, and Piacenza, who have always and devoutly believed in the Servant of God's Holiness, and who now await being able to venerate her in the glory of the altars.

Rome, 15 December 2006.

Sister Angela Florio, FSA,

Salvatore Orsi Promotor Fiscalis petit et instat ut testes a Causae Postulatore inducti et inducendi, necnon testes et contestes ex officio vocanti priusquam interrogentur super articulis, sejunctim et diligentes examinentur super interrogatoriis a se propositis praevio juramento justa formam Decretorum S. 1. In primis moneatur quilibet testis cuiuscumque gradus, status, sexus et conditionis de vi et gravitate juramenti, praesertim hisce in causis qua sunt ex mayoribus in Ecclesia Dei, et de poenis contra perjuros.

2. Interrogetur quilibet testis de nomine, cognomine, aetate, patria, domicilio, parentibus, gradu, statu et professione, deque aliis circumstantiis ad testem pertinentibus.

3. Interrogetur: an quolibet anno duplici Ecclesiae praecepto satisfecerit de Sacramentali confessione et Sacra Sinaxi tempore Paschali recipienda, et utrum ad eadem Sacramenta alias per annum accedere consueverit.

4. Interrogetur: an fuerit unquam ob aliquod crimen inquisitus, accusatus, processui subjectus, et si affirmaverit dicat quodnam ob crimen, coram quo judice, quo tempore, an semel vel pluries, et an secuta sit absolutio vel condemnatio.

5. Interrogetur: an aliqua de causa fuerit unquam excommunicatus vel alteri ecclesiasticae censurae subjectus. Num fuerit absolutus, vel adhuc in eadem censura permaneat.

6. Interrogetur: an unquam ab aliquo fuerit instinctus de iis quae sunt deponenda, et utrum ad testimonium ferendum inducatur aliquia lucri, commodi aut honoris spe, vel metu damni, aut quovis alio temporali et humano fine, vel potius ob zelum gloriae et honoris Dei.

7. Interrogetur: an noverit vel nominari audiverit Dei Famulam Sororem Annam Orsi a SS. Salvatore ex Congregatione Filiarum S. Annae. Si testis affirmet, dicat ubi, quamdiu, quando, quoties, a quibus, qua occasione, ad quem finem.

8. Interrogetur: an peculiari devotione necne prosequatur dictam Dei Famulam, et qua de causa, an exoptet vel curet eius Beatificationem, cur et quomodo, referendo adjuncta, omnia quae necessaria et opportuna videbuntur.

9. Interrogetur: an sciat vel dici audiverit quo anno, mense, quo die quove loco Serva Dei Soror Anna Orsi lucem adspexerit, quibus acta parentibus, quaenam eorum nomina, cognomina, patria, fortuna, fides, moves. An et quando Dei Famula baptisma susceperit et confirmationis Sacramentum. Dicat etiam quae fuerit prima institutio Servae Dei, et a quibus eam acceperit, referendo adjuncta omnia omnesque circumstantias cum suae scientiae causa.

10. Interrogetur: an sciat vel dici audiverit quam rationem tenuerit Dei Famula in sua pueritia, utrum pietati necne vocaverit, utrum parentibus subjecta et moderatoribus, utrum argumenta vel signa praebuerit futurae Sanctitatis, quae. Et quomodo, referendo omnia ajuncta et omnes circumstantias cum suae scientiae causa.

11. Interrogetur: an sciat vel dici audiverit utrum Dei Famula adolescentiam semper in paterna domo transegerit, et si dixerit, uti ferunt articuli, eam aliquando cum suis avunculis moratam fuisse, dicat qua de causa, quomodo sese gesserit, quomodo pietatem coluerit, referendo omnia adjuncta rerum, locorum, personarum, temporis, omnesque circumstantias cum scientiae causa.

12. Interrogetur: an sciat vel dici audiverit quinam fuerit vitae status a Serva Dei electus, et si dixerit fuisse statum religiosum, dicat an eum amplexa libere sit, an contra parentum voluntatem, qua in urbe, quo in instituto, quo anno, referendo adjuncta omnia, uti supra.

13. Interrogetur: an sciat vel dici audiverit qua ratione Dei Famula tirocinium suum exegerit, an et quae in eo praebuerit virtutum et sanctitatis exempla, et an religiosam professionem hilari animo emiserit, quando, ubi, qua aetate, referendo adjuncta omnia uti supra.

14. Interrogetur testis: an sciat vel dici audiverit utrum Dei Famula semper in una domo vitam duxerit, et si negaverit, dicat quibus aliis in locis morata sit, qua de causa, quibus vel rationibus ad alia loca aliasque civitates missa fuerit, a quibus, quo tempore, quae opera in aliis exgerit, et si discerit eam missam fuisse ad fundandas alias congregationis domos vel ad alias regendas, dicat qua ratione haec omnia peregerit, quam famam sibi acquisiverit, an recte et prudenter gubernaverit, referendo distincte et ordinate rerum et factorum adjuncta cum omnibus circumstantiis temporis et personarum, et suae scientiae causa.

15. Interrogetur testis: an sciat vel dici audiverit utrum Dei Famula injurias et persecutiones tulerit, et si affirmaverit dicat quibus de causis, a quibus personis et praecise an a saecularibus vel superioribus et religiosis, quo tempore, quo in loco, an dictae contradictiones et injuriae quas testes recensebunt fuerint graver et multiplices, an iis Dei Famula causam praebuerit, vel e contra. Si discerit testis minime eas promeritam fuisse Dei Famulam, dicat qua ratione eas pertulerit, an patienti vel irato animo, an ii qui eas contradictiones inferebant agnoverunt et confessi sunt innocentiam et patientiam Servae Dei, referendo adjuncta omnia uti supra.

16. Interrogetur testis: an sciat vel dici audiverit quaenam fuerit agendi ratio quam tenuit Dei Famula dum vixit, utrum semper observaverit mandata Dei et Ecclesia, necnon ea omnia quibus obligabatur ratione status religiosi, quomodo regulas Instituti servaverit, quae fuerit aliarum religiosarum ea de re opinio et famam, referendo adjuncta ect.

In hoc interrogatorio maxima continetur Processus pars et ratio ideoque oportet, quam possibile est, enuere a testibus omnia qua ipsi sciant, et maxime in responsione abundare.

17. Interrogetur testis: an sciat vel dici audiverit an Dei Serva christianas virtutes necne excoluerit et exercuerit, theologales nempe et cardinales, caeterasque quae iis adnexae sunt, et an usque ad mortem in iis perseveraverit. Si testis affirmet, interrogetur singillatim de unaquaque virtute, et primum de fide eiusque actibus, quomodo et quibus actibus eam Dei Famula exercuerit, omnia referendo diffuse et ordinate quae relationem habent ad unamquanque virtutem, postea de spe, de charitate in Deum et proximum, deinde de cardinalibus, prudentia, justitia, temperantia, fortitudine, de humilitate, de paupertate, castitate et obedientia testes distincte et singillatim interrogentur referantque omnium virtutum singulos actus, et facta atque argumenta omnia quibus ipsi judicent Dei Famulam claruisse virtutibus quas referunt, et suae scientiae causam.

18. Interrogetur testis: an sciat vel dici audiverit quo gradu Dei Famula recensitas virtutes exercuerit, an heroico et sublimi, vel potius communi. Si testis primum affirmet, dicat an id contigerit de omnibus, vel tantum de aliquibus et quibus. Dicat etiam quae sit, sua sententia, virtus heroica et in quo consistat, et quibus factis quibusque argumentis moveatur ut sentiat virtutes omnes vel aliquias Servae Dei fuisse heroicas.

19. Interrogetur: an sciat vel dici audiverit utrum Dei Famula aliquid dixerit, scripserit vel fecerit quod christianis virtutibus adversetur, vel in sui laudem verterit, referendo argumenta ect.

20. Interrogetur: an sciat vel dici audiverit utrum Dei Famula supernis donis et coelestibus charismatibus insignita fuerit, puta prophetiae, cordium scrutationis, extasum, visionum aliorumque. Si testis affirmet, dicat etiam quaenam ea fuerint dona, referat omnia facta quae comprobarunt eadem dona, et quidnam alii senserint de iisdem. Interrogetur etiam an Dei Famula de iis locuta unquam sit, et si affirmet, dicat an id egerit vel ex necessitate eadem aperiendi superioribus vel confessariis, vel ex utilitate proximorum, vel de instinctu, vel contra ad suam gloriam captandam, referendo adjuncta omnia etc.

21. Interrogetur: num sciat vel dici audiverit utrum Dei Serva intercedente, dum viveret, aliquod miraculum Deus patraverit vel gratiam, referendo adjuncta omnia illius facti vel gratiae, et hominum opinionem, cum suae scientiae causa.

22. Interrogetur: num sciat vel dici audiverit quo die, mense, anno, ubi et qua infirmitate Dei Famula mortem aberit. Dicat quando infirmitas inceperit, quamdiu et qua ratione perduraverit, dicat distincte et enucleate qua ratione Dei Famula in hac postrema infirmitate sese gesserit, an ecclesiae sacramenta, necne, ipsa quaesierit, et quae, quando, quomodo; describat actus religionis et pietatis quibus Dei Famula operam dedit, enarret virtutum exercitationem, hilaritatem et laetitiam in extremis vita diebus, dicat an tentationes necne pertuberit in extrema lucta, et quomodo Serva Dei sese gesteris in iisdem referendo adjuncta omnia ect.

23. Interrogetur: an sciat vel dici audiverit ubinam cadaver Servae Dei positum et tumulatum fuerit, an ad illud invisendum concursus populi fuerit et qua de causa, an raptae fuerint an exquisitae reliquiae, qua fuerit hominum tunc opinio, qua voces, qui sermones de Serva Dei, cuius generis fuerit populus qui accurrit, an nobiles etiam viri et qui an aliquid mirabile acciderit in illis circumstantiis, referendo adjuncta omnia ect.

24. Interrogetur testis: an sciat vel dici audiverit ubinam cadaver Servae Dei tumulatum fuerit, quae sit sepulchri ratio, an aliquam praeseferat inscriptionem et quam, an recognitio aliqua exuviarum Servae Dei unquam sit habita, referendo ect.

25. Interrogetur testis: an sciat vel dici audiverit utrum populus accurrat ad invisendum et venerandum sepulchrum Servae Dei, qua de causa, quando inceperit concursus iste, et quibus personis constituatur, an e plebe tantum homines, vel etiam viri docti et prudentes, et qui fuerint isti, quae sint hominum pietatis significationes ad sepulchrum Servae Dei, an concursus iste perseveret et auctus sit, vel an contra diminutus, intermissus, cur, quomodo, quando. Dicat demum an Servae Dei cadaver semper eodem loco manserit, et ubi ad praesens asservatur referendo adjuncta omnia ect.

26. Interrogetur: an sciat vel dici audiverit quae opinio et fama fuerit de vita ac virtutibus Servae Dei dum ipsa viveret, et si dixerit famam fuisse et viguisse sanctitatis, dicat qua de causa haec fama inceperit, penes quos viguerit et quibus in locis, referendo adjuncta omnia ect.

27. Interrogetur testis: an sciat vel dici audiverit quae fama sit et quae hominum opinio de Serva Dei post eius obitum, et si dixerit esse famam sanctitatis, interrogetur quibus de causis haec fama vigeat, penes quos homine, an universalis sit et penes saniorem populi partem, quibus in locis vel civitatibus vigeat, an incrementa assumat, dicat quibus modis vel quibus rationibus homines exprimant ac manifestent hanc opinionem sanctitatis, an invocando auxilium Servae Dei, an expetendo eius reliquias, narrando et extollendo eius virtutes, vel aliis modis qui a testibus referentur cum omnibus adjunctis ect.

28. Interrogeur testis: an sciat vel dici audiverit utrum aliquid dictum, factum vel scriptum fuerit contra virtutes Servae Dei vel sanctitatis famam vel dum ipsa viveret, vel post eius obitum. Si testis affirmet, interrogetur de hominibus qui haec gerint, dicat eorum nomina et ubi commoventur, qua de causa Serva Dei obtrectaverint, quomodo eos judicet aut judicaverit prudentum hominum opinio, referendo quae sint obiecta contra Dei Famulam, cum suis adjunctis etc.

29. Interrogetur testis: an sciat vel dici audiverit utrum vita functa Dei Famula, eius, necne, intercessione ab omnipotenti Deo aliqua gratia concessa sit vel patiatum miraculum. Si affirmet, dicat quid sit gratia et quid miraculum et in quo differant. Postea fuse et distincte exponat omnia et singula facta quae testis judicat esse miracula vel gratias obtentas intercedente Dei Famula, describat exacte morbos et curationem, adhibitam, dicat medicorum et adsistentium opinionem, dicat quando fuerit invocata Serva Dei, an immediate habita fuerit sanatio perfecta, an e contra lapsu temporis et successive, et quot diebus, recensendo nomina contestium et omnia factorum adjuncta et circumstantias ect.

30. Interrogetur denique: an praeterea quae deposuit, aliud habeat attendum, vel delendum, vel corrigendum, sive quod deinceps menti occurrerit, sive de quo speciatim non fuit interrogatus, recolendo obligationem qua tenetur aperiendi omnia et nihil occultandi, nec sub praetextu quod de eo specialiter non fuit interrogatus.

Et haec cum facultate addendi ect. pronti expedire in Domino videbitur.

Canonicus Petrus Boccone

Subpromotor Fidei

I

Each witness, of whatever condition and standing, is to be warned about the gravity and sanctity of the oath, which is to be taken according to the prescribed formula.

II

The witness is to be asked for full personal details, profession, and any other personal data useful for identifying them.

III

The witness is to be asked:

1. whether they are bound to the Servant of God by some natural or spiritual tie (kinship, membership in the same religious Institute, esteem, etc.).

2. what motive moves them to testify.

3. whether they have received instructions or suggestions regarding their deposition.

IV

The witness is to be asked what is the source of their own knowledge of the Servant of God (for example: extrajudicial testimonies, biographies, etc.) and to provide useful indications.

V

The witness is to be asked whether there exist (which, and where) writings of the Servant of God, and whether they know their content.

VI

The witness is to be asked whether there exist, or whether they are in possession of, documents useful to the cause (if so: they are to be invited to produce them in the original or in a certified copy).

VII

1. What particulars about the Servant of God's life does the witness consider most relevant, or at least which ones are most present in their memory?

2. What particulars do they know about the various virtues the Servant of God practiced?

Do they consider that the Servant of God practiced these virtues to a heroic degree?

3. In Sicily, what particular activities did the Servant of God carry out, and how were they regarded?

4. What, in the witness's judgment, are the characteristic notes of the Servant of God's spirituality?

What message could the Servant of God give to contemporary society?

5. Does the witness hold devotion to the Servant of God (if so: how and why).

6. When did the Servant of God's reputation for holiness arise, and how and where did it develop, in ecclesiastical circles and among the faithful?

7. What opinion regarding the Servant of God's reputation for holiness was held within the religious Congregation of the "Daughters of St. Anne"?

8. Are there people or writings opposed to the Servant of God's reputation for holiness and to the cause of beatification?

VIII

1. Where was the Servant of God's body buried, and where is it presently located?

2. Does the Servant of God's tomb constitute a place of attraction for the faithful, and for what purpose?

3. At the Servant of God's tomb or in other places, has the witness noticed any possible manifestation of undue public cult?

Have images of the Servant of God been produced?

4. Does the witness know whether, through the Servant of God's intercession, miracles or graces have been obtained (if so, let them report the particulars).

IX

Having heard the deposition read back, does the witness have anything to add, remove, or correct?
