Name, date and place of birth: Rosalia Bertuzzi, in religion Sister Anna Battistina, born in 1849 in Settima di Gossolengo (Piacenza).

State and profession: Religious of the Daughters of St. Anne, Provincial Superior.

Quality of the witness: Eyewitness.

Witness's age when she knew the Servant of God: about 24 years.

Servant of God's age when the witness knew her: about 31 years.

Witness's age at the time of deposition: 57 years.

Length of acquaintance and its reason: The witness knew the Servant of God in Piacenza, as a member of the same Institute; afterwards, when transferred to Palermo, she visited her assiduously, living for some time in the same house and resorting to her very often on account of her office.

Observations on the witness, the scope, and the content of the deposition: The witness provides valuable information about the religious life of the Servant of God and the setbacks borne with serenity and fortitude. Ad 2 interr., proc. pag. 157, testis respondit:

§ 44
General information on the witness.

My name is Rosalia Bertuzzi, in religion Sister Anna Battistina, 57 years of age, born in the Municipality of Settimo di Gossolengo, province of Piacenza, residing in Palermo, Via Alessandro Paternostro, Briuccia Palace. My parents were named Luigi Bertuzzi and Giuseppa Ferri; I am Provincial Superior of the Daughters of St. Anne in Palermo.

Ad 6: I have come to testify for Sister Anna del SS. Salvatore spontaneously, upon invitation: and no one has suggested or imposed on me what I must answer.

§ 45
Scope of knowledge.

Ad 7: I knew the Servant of God on various occasions: first in Piacenza, and afterwards I dealt with her for a good while here in Palermo, when, having been assigned as Superior of the Sisters in this Civic Hospital of St. Xavier, I had to live for a time in the Central House, where the Servant of God acted as Provincial Superior. It was she who then accompanied me to the Hospital and installed me in my office. Afterwards I had many occasions to approach her for reasons connected with the exercise of my said office, whether for advice, for help, etc.

§ 46
Great esteem for the Servant of God.

Ad 8: I had great veneration for the Servant of God while she lived, for her virtues: and after her death, even more, and I have commended myself to her in all the needs and difficulties of life. I too desire that the Servant of God be raised to the honours of the Altars.

§ 47
Piety and special devotion from childhood.

Ad 10: Of her childhood I know nothing de visu, but I have heard it said, especially by a religious sister of hers, likewise in our Institute of the Daughters of St. Anne, now mistress of novices in Rome, that the Servant of God, even from that age, showed something special for her piety and devotion; a withdrawn and mortified life.

Ad 12: The Servant of God entered the Institute of the Daughters of St. Anne with a true vocation in Piacenza, where she took the religious habit.

§ 48
Various places where the Servant of God worked.

Ad 14: From Piacenza she was sent to Florence, where she lived a long time, and where she had much to suffer. Then she came to Palermo to found the Institute here, with other religious. As soon as she arrived she drew the goodwill and devotion of the whole city, and especially of some distinguished persons, such as the Princess of Fitalia, Mrs. Pittalà, and others.

Ad 15: While the Servant of God was in Florence as Superior, she had much to suffer, both from the economic hardship of the House, which was deprived of means of subsistence, so that she was obliged to beg, and from some slander that certain ill-disposed persons leveled against her innocent life. This I heard said.

§ 49
Showed deep humility when slandered.
§ 50
Was recognised as innocent.

On this point I add that I know, from having heard it said, that the slander leveled against her was aired in Florence on the occasion when, in Piacenza, the Superiors of the various Houses had gathered for the Spiritual Exercises. It was said that the Servant of God had spoken in the Community words lacking in respect towards the Foundress Mother and her family; so much so that it was proposed to take away her veil and send her away. Informed of this, the Servant of God refused to defend herself, but, bowing her head in true humility, said: "If God wills this humiliation for me, I am ready to undergo it." Matters being thus clarified, and her innocence recognised, she regained the esteem of the Foundress Mother and the Sisters, so that she was afterwards sent as Superior to Palermo.

§ 51
Observant of the Law of God and the Rule.

Ad 16: I can attest, both from having heard it said and from my own experience, that the Servant of God was most observant not only of what concerns the law of God and the Precepts of the Church but also of the duties and rules of the holy Institute.

§ 52
Observed all the virtues.

Ad 17: I answer in general that everything contained in this Interrogatory and concerning all the virtues, theological, cardinal, of religion, etc., the Servant of God observed faithfully, I having had many occasions to know this.

§ 53
Practiced the virtues in heroic degree.

Ad 18: I can attest to having witnessed the practice of many of the Servant of God's virtues, which, to my mind, have something heroic about them. And by heroism I mean a virtue that is above the ordinary.

§ 54
Humility.

Ad 19: The Servant of God's humility was such that she was incapable, not merely of writing or saying things that would redound to her praise, but even of thinking them.

Ad 20: Of the gifts of God the Servant of God may have received, I could say much, also from my own personal experience. But I intend to speak specifically when I am examined on the Articles: something I meant to do and will do when the particular virtues and their heroic degree are discussed.

§ 55
Precious death of the Servant of God.

Ad 22: The Servant of God's death occurred on 7 June 1885 at 10:30 in the evening, a Sunday. I was present at her death. She received the last sacraments at her own request. She was quite glad to die. Her death was truly precious for the calm and tranquility that accompanied it.

§ 56
The Servant of God's remains greatly venerated.
§ 57
Burial and reputation for holiness.

Ad 23, proc. p. 162: After the Servant of God's death, in preparing her body, as is customary, I noticed that on her chest, on the side of the heart, there was something like an imprint, a shape impressed as though some red-hot iron plate had been applied there: this was my impression, which, out of reverence, I kept secret, and which I disclosed to the Mother General when she asked me about the Servant of God's precious death. The body, dressed in the religious habit, was laid out in the mortuary room, and remained so until the next day around four in the afternoon, she having died the previous evening. Many people came when news of her death spread: persons of standing came to venerate the body, and asked for keepsakes and relics. I was the first to take for myself the veil she wore on her head, and I cut off some of her hair. Everyone said with one voice that a saint had died, and extolled her truly admirable virtues. When the body was afterwards carried to the Cemetery of St. Ursula, many gentlemen sent their carriages as a tribute to the Servant of God.

§ 58
Identification of the Servant of God's body.

Ad 24: The Lady Princess of Fitalia would have liked the Servant of God's body to be buried in a tomb of its own, and gave instructions for a suitable burial place to be built: but at the time no one thought to ask the Curia to have it placed in a place of deposit. Thus, another Sister having died the day after the Servant of God's death, that sister's body had to be buried in the same grave as the other. However, after about two and a half years, it was decided to place the Servant of God's body in a place of deposit; this came about especially through the initiative and effort of the Princess of Fitalia. Indeed, the party went to the site with the ecclesiastical Tribunal and, the body having been exhumed in the presence also of our Foundress Mother, who had come specially, and of many Sisters and distinguished Ladies, the identification was carried out. A glass tube was found in the coffin containing a document signed by many people. At the initiative of the same Princess of Fitalia a Latin inscription was placed above the tomb and it was enclosed with an iron railing. The records of this identification are kept in the Curia.

Ad 25: In our Institute there is great devotion towards the Servant of God, and people always, and often, go to her tomb to venerate her and to pray in order to obtain some special grace.

§ 59
Reputation for holiness in life and after death.

Ad 26-27: While she lived, Sister Anna del Salvatore enjoyed a reputation as a holy religious, and everyone held her as such; for her virtues, despite her reserve, showed themselves quite clearly and plainly.

This reputation for holiness of the Servant of God did not fade after her death; rather, it spread and grew not only here in Palermo and in our Houses in Sicily, but also outside them; for in the Mother House this devotion towards the Servant of God is widespread.

Ad 28: Of writings against the Servant of God's virtues I have no knowledge. Yes, she had some contradictions and defamatory slanders; but these were later dispelled, and of them I have already spoken in an earlier Interrogatory; and this was while she was alive. After her death not a word was ever heard against her.

§ 60
Miraculous events that occurred.

Ad 29: As I understand it, by a miracle I mean an extraordinary event that is above the laws of nature; whereas by a grace I mean a cure that followed as a result. Many miraculous events have occurred through the Servant of God's intercession, which I would not know how to relate here in exact detail, but which people attribute to something extraordinary.

Ad 30: As to what I declared above, I have nothing to add, remove, or change. I reserve what else I might say for when the Articles are dealt with.

§ 61
Care for her younger little brothers and sisters.

Et expleto examine super Interrogatoriis, deventum est ad examen super Articulis, testis dixit:

Ad 2, proc. p. 166: Of the care the Servant of God had for her little brothers and sisters, I heard it from a priest who knew her.

Ad 3: I heard it said of the Servant of God's piety from her earliest years.

§ 62
Spirit of piety from childhood.

Ad 8: Of this I heard talk among us, namely that she never wished to marry.

Ad 10: Of the time of the Servant of God's novitiate I heard it said that she rejoiced at her clothing.

Ad 12: Of the Servant of God's abilities I heard it said.

§ 63
Sacrifices endured during her travels.

Ad 15: Of the journeys she bore in the various foundations in Sicily, I know of the sacrifices she had to suffer, which are truly marked by heroism: especially since in those days the means of travelling comfortably, as now, were lacking.

§ 64
Practiced the virtues for the benefit of the needy.

Ad 16: As far as I know, I can attest that the Servant of God had to bear great sacrifices in the direction of the various houses and to practice the most exalted virtues for the benefit of the needy.

§ 65
Admirable faith.

Ad 17: I can attest that the Servant of God's faith was truly admirable.

Ad 22: As to the Servant of God's dispositions regarding her wish that the faith of God spread everywhere, I can attest to this for the time I knew her.

§ 66
Adorer of the Blessed Sacrament.

Ad 23: As to devotion to the Blessed Sacrament, I attest that the Servant of God was a true adorer, and the same as regards the Most Holy Virgin, St. Anne, and the Saints of God in general.

§ 67
Respect for the Lord's ministers.

Ad 24: I know that the Servant of God respected the Lord's Ministers and was most devoted to the Pope, to whose slightest word she declared herself ready to obey.

Ad 25: I can attest that the Servant of God was most devoted to the Souls in Purgatory.

§ 68
Instructed others in the faith.

Ad 26: It is quite true that the Servant of God had great zeal in instructing the young women under her care in matters concerning the faith.

§ 69
Animated by hope.

Ad 27: Unfortunately [sic] it is true that she was animated by this virtue of hope.

§ 70
Had great trust in everything and never lost heart.

Ad 29: I know personally of the great confidence the Servant of God had in everything.

§ 71
Serenity in the face of death.

Ad 30: As to the Servant of God's inward feelings of confidence, I can say nothing; but that she was not cast down or discouraged by the obstacles opposing her works of zeal, that I can attest.

Ad 31: As to her confidence in God at the point of death, or as to her tranquility, I attest to this with certainty.

§ 72
Was always ablaze with divine love.

Ad 32: Of the love the Servant of God bore for God, I can attest to it: she was always ablaze with this divine love.

Ad 33: As to her observance of the Divine Precepts and of every other obligation of hers, I can attest to this.

§ 73
Ardour in receiving Holy Communion.

Ad 34: I can attest to nothing regarding the Servant of God's earliest years: but I know with what ardour she received Holy Communion every day while in Religion.

§ 74
Spent whole nights before the Blessed Sacrament.

Ad 36: It is also [sic] true what is said of her devotion to the Blessed Sacrament: she spent whole nights before the Tabernacle, in a true spirit of most loving ecstasy.

§ 75
Generosity in suffering for God.

Ad 37: As to her generosity in suffering for God, I attest to this from my own experience.

Ad 38: This too I can attest, since she was always intent on acquiring every virtue.

§ 76
Serene joy in the face of death.

Ad 39: As to the Servant of God's dispositions at the point of death, I can attest to this, having been present at her death: it is quite true that she was glad to go to be reunited with her Divine Spouse.

§ 77
Devotion to Our Lady.

Ad 40: Of the Servant of God's devotion to Our Lady, I know and attest to this. She had a little image of Our Lady towards which she had a particular devotion.

§ 78
Concern for her fellow Sisters.

Ad 42: I also know personally of what she did for her fellow religious Sisters, in comforting them, helping them, and relieving them.

§ 79
Zeal for poor and endangered girls.

Ad 43: I heard it said of what the Servant of God did for girls, whether endangered or poor, and of the zeal she had for their welfare.

§ 80
Self-denial in caring for the sick.

Ad 44: It is true what is said in this Article, that is, of her self-denial in attending to the sick, even the filthiest and most wretched.

Ad 45: I never heard from the Servant of God's lips a word that could offend charity towards the neighbour.

§ 81
Spirit of sacrifice for the neighbour.

Ad 46: I attest, as the truth, that the Servant of God was animated by this spirit of sacrifice for the good of her neighbours.

Ad 47: Of her equal spirit towards her neighbours, by which she made no distinction of persons, I know and attest to this.

§ 82
Gave proof of admirable prudence.

Ad 48: In the time I knew her, I can attest that, on so many occasions, she gave many proofs of admirable prudence.

Ad 49: This prudence in the choice of the religious state speaks for itself.

Ad 50: As to the generality of the matter, that is, the fact that the Servant of God was sent to govern various Houses, which proves the Servant of God's prudence, this seems a clear thing.

§ 83
The offices entrusted to her show her prudence.

Ad 51: It is a fact that the Servant of God was named Provincial of all the houses of Sicily at the General Chapter: this shows the confidence all the Chapter members had in her.

§ 84
Was endowed with the spirit of counsel.

Ad 52: This confidence the administrators had in her prudence in the various Houses is also known to me.

§ 85
Justice, respect, and courtesy.

Ad 53: It is true, and known to me, that she had this spirit of counsel, by which her fellow Sisters received from her direction and comfort.

Ad 54: This spirit of rendering to each what was due was habitual in her: respect for all and social courtesies were her special character.

§ 86
Gratitude towards the Lord.

Ad 55: The Servant of God was grateful to the Lord and always thanked Him, not only for the vocation to the faith but also for the religious state.

§ 87
Instilled in her fellow Sisters a spirit of gratitude.

Ad 56: This spirit of gratitude towards God she instilled in the souls of the Sisters, whom she always urged to give thanks to God for the benefits received.

Ad 57: Speaking of the Servant of God's clothing, I can attest nothing.

§ 88
Cared for the decorum of the house of God.
§ 89
Was constant in the practice of justice.

Ad 58: Truly the Servant of God had great zeal for the decorum of the House of God, both for the decent cleanliness and tidiness of the church and the sacred furnishings, and for the composure she wished to be kept in church.

Ad 59: It is true that the Servant of God never harmed anyone, neither by failing in truth nor by failing in justice, that is, in the interest of third parties.

§ 90
Showed extraordinary fortitude amid adversities.

Ad 60: The spirit of fortitude amid adversities is woven throughout her whole life in a truly extraordinary way, although she seemed cheerful and content.

Ad 64: I heard it said that the Servant of God had to suffer scorn and ill-treatment not here but in Florence, where she received grave insults and outrages, to the point of being driven off with stones when going to beg alms.

§ 91
Suffered ill-treatment and persecutions.

Ad 65, proc. p. 175: Of ill-treatment and persecutions suffered by the Servant of God from outside, in the exercise of her offices and of her zeal for the good of the people, I could not attest; as regards the Community, I have already spoken of this in dealing with what she suffered at the General Chapter in Florence.

§ 92
Her patience and fortitude aroused admiration.

Ad 66: This Article I can confirm, having been present at the Servant of God's last illness and death. Her patience and fortitude aroused the admiration of all who attended her, myself included.

§ 93
Was most temperate in food.

Ad 67: I heard everything said in this Article about the Servant of God's temperance in food, more than what she actually preferred [sic]. However, I know de visu that, going sometimes to the Briuccia house, where she was Superior, and finding her at table with the other Sisters, I saw her with leaves of greens on her plate; but the kind that are thrown away. I recall that once she came to the Hospital of St. Xavier, where I was Superior. We were at recreation and sweets were being handed out: she took a little out of obedience, but perhaps went to bring it up afterwards, since she withdrew from us immediately.

§ 94
Spent the night in prayer.

Ad 68: I know the Servant of God had no bed of her own: she took her rest seated in a chair; but for the most part she spent the night before the Blessed Sacrament.

Ad 69: Of this particular detail narrated in this Article, of a religious having come upon her before the Blessed Sacrament, I know nothing; but I believe it quite possible.

§ 95
Was indulgent with the Sisters and austere with herself.

Ad 70: I confirm what is said in this Article about her indulgence and kindness in dealing with the Sisters, as I also confirm her austerity towards herself.

§ 96
Used instruments of penance especially on Fridays.

Ad 72: I know what is said here about the use of instruments of penance, which she kept hidden; but that, one of them having been found on the occasion of her illness, she blushed.

Ad 73: What is said in this Article, about her extraordinary use of instruments of penance every Friday, I have heard said, and I can attest that at times I myself noticed, in her movements on Fridays, signs indicating bodily suffering.

§ 97
Kept calm even in the most difficult moments.

Ad 74: I never saw her disturbed or uneasy, even on extraordinary occasions that should have made her greatly angry.

§ 98
Her love of poverty was known to all.

Ad 75: The Servant of God's love of poverty is known to all: that she wore the plainest clothing is most certain; so much so that at her death her clothes were found truly meager.

Ad 76: I know very well that she never made any waste of the Community's goods and belongings, and with holy ingenuity sought to economise even in things that would otherwise have had no further use; as they say, keeping the wick to make the stamens of flowers, etc.

§ 99
Her room had no bed.

Ad 77: Of the poverty of her room, which lacked even necessary things, even a bed, which she said would have been a luxury for her.

Ad 78: This fact, that the Servant of God travelled by train in the livestock car for lack of money, I heard said.

§ 100
Instilled in the Sisters the spirit of poverty.

Ad 79: This manner of speaking was her habit, that is, she liked to know she ate by alms, and so she begged; and this spirit of poverty she instilled in the Sisters, to whom she said, going to the refectory, that they should consider themselves poor women receiving their food by alms.

Ad 80: As to the Servant of God's love for chastity, I can speak of her reserve in dealing with people.

§ 101
Observed chastity.

Ad 81: I never heard from the Servant of God's lips a word that even slightly suggested anything that could harm the splendour of this beautiful virtue.

§ 102
Her exhortations on chastity were edifying.

Ad 82: I know everything said here about her frequent reception of the sacraments and of everything else that served to guard holy purity.

Ad 83: These exhortations on this beautiful virtue, made to the Sisters, were a truly edifying thing for the whole Community.

§ 103
Was obedient even to the point of sacrifice.

Ad 84: The Servant of God was most obedient, even to the point of sacrifice. And this I know on many occasions.

Ad 85: This spirit of conformity to the Mother General's wishes was also known to all, and I attest to it.

§ 104
Obeyed promptly and always.

Ad 86: Her obedience towards the Mother General, even in things disagreeable to her, we know and attest.

Ad 87: This fact of her obedience, imposed by the Mother General without the latter knowing of the Servant of God's gravely ill state, is such as must cause amazement. She left with a fever of 104°F. She went, settled the matter; but, back in Palermo, she took to her bed, from which she never rose again.

Ad 88: It is true that, in her last illness, she obeyed the doctor's and the Sisters' instructions, both as to medicines and as to the manner of carrying out the prescriptions.

§ 105
Made obedience seem pleasant and easy.

Ad 89: Truly, all of us who kept her company would have wished to imitate her in this noble virtue of obedience, so much did she make it appear pleasant and easy.

§ 106
Considered herself the last of all.

Ad 90: The Servant of God's whole life is sown with feelings of true humility. She often said she was the last and quite unnecessary; that others would have known how to do better than she; that she was the last in the house, and called herself the donkey of the Community.

Ad 91: Of the Servant of God's expressions of humility, one can say that it was her whole life. It was its mirror.

Ad 92: Not having lived together with the Servant of God in the same house, I could not attest to what is said in this Article, namely how she preferred the Sisters' comfort to her own: nonetheless I have heard this said and I attest to it, as well as the fact of choosing the vilest things for herself.

Ad 93: Of herself she took no account at all, I attest this.

§ 107
Felt mortified by words of praise.

Ad 94: I know and attest that when we spoke words of praise to her, she was mortified by it and instead spoke of herself in words of contempt.

Ad 95: These things said in this Article, about the way she accepted scorn, I heard from other Sisters.

§ 108
Instilled in everyone feelings of humility.

Ad 96: That she instilled in everyone feelings of humility, I myself could feel, to my own great edification and that of others.

§ 109
Was seen absorbed in prayer and in ecstasy.

Ad 97: I heard it said that the Servant of God fell into ecstasy, that she had been found absorbed in God in prayer, to the point that it was hard to rouse her, and so many other things of a supernatural character.

§ 110
Foretold her own death and that of a Sister.

Ad 98: Of this Article I attest only what is known to me personally, namely the fact of the foretelling of imminent death announced for herself and for another Sister whom she had gone to visit, shortly before her last illness.

§ 111
Foretold the recovery of a gravely ill Sister.

Ad 99: The prediction mentioned here, concerning a gravely ill Sister, a certain Sister Alberica, that she would soon recover while the Servant of God herself would die, is known to me and happened exactly so.

§ 112
Prodigiously obtained money.

Ad 100: This fact of the increase of the two hundred lire she needed, I heard recounted by a Sister, who relates that, a young postulant having come to her with an envelope containing eighty lire, the Servant of God told her she needed more than double that, and that she should go put the envelope in front of the Sacrament, behind the Altar Card, and pray. The fact was that, on taking back the envelope, it was found with two hundred lire more.

§ 113
Enjoyed a reputation as a religious of holy life.

Ad 103, proc. p. 182: I attest and confirm what is said in this Article, that is, the opinion held of her as a religious of holy life while she was alive.

§ 114
Was admired as an angel in attending the sick.

Ad 104: I can attest, as to this Article, that truly, wherever the Servant of God went to attend the sick, she was admired and venerated as a true angel from Heaven.

§ 115
Many people, even noble ones, asked her for advice and prayers.

Ad 105: I know and attest that many people, even of the highest aristocracy of Palermo, often came to visit the Servant of God, either to ask advice or to obtain through her prayers some special grace, so great was the opinion commonly held of her truly singular virtues.

§ 116
Easily obtained alms thanks to the opinion held of her.

Ad 106: It is true what is said in this Article: it is quite [sic] true that as soon as the Servant of God presented herself to people to ask for whatever she needed, her mere presence was enough for her to easily obtain everything, and this, I say, always on account of the reputation for holiness she had with everyone.

§ 117
Was held in veneration among the laity and the Clergy of Palermo.

Ad 107: Of the veneration in which the Servant of God was held in all the Houses where she was in the capacity of superior, I attest to this fully, as it is also known to me. Just as I attest to the veneration in which she was held among the laity and the clergy of our city of Palermo. I recall, in this regard, what happened on the occasion of our Community's settling in the Briuccia house. The house of St. Mark, where our Institute was received on our first coming to Palermo, having become too small as it grew noticeably, another, larger place was thought of. And the Servant of God, whether by a natural impulse or a supernatural revelation I could not say, presented herself to Msgr. Gaetano Briuccia to obtain some space in his various houses which he owned in Palermo. She then went to Fr. Briuccia and set forth her request; but Fr. Briuccia at first refused, saying he had no houses available. Then the Servant of God knelt before him and, in a pleading tone and with hands joined, said: "Monsignor, it is not I who come, but it is the Most Holy Virgin who sends me to you." These words, her confident and pleading tone, moved Fr. Briuccia, and on the spot, having called his servant, he said to him: "Take the keys to the upper mezzanine, open it, and you, Mother Provincial, see if it suits you; you may inhabit it from now on." And indeed that apartment became our dwelling for several years. But afterwards, again out of consideration for the Servant of God, Msgr. Briuccia granted her a more comfortable apartment, which we still inhabit.

§ 118
With her humility, obtained the use of the dwelling from Monsignor Briuccia.

§ 119
Esteemed by all throughout her life.

Ad 108: It is quite [sic] true that the Servant of God enjoyed great esteem throughout the City of Palermo, and that this esteem continued until her death.

§ 120
Admirable patience and serenity in her last illness.

Ad 109: Everything said in this Article is true. I too was present at the Servant of God's last illness and I too could admire, with my other fellow Sisters, the beautiful virtues she showed: patience, resignation, and the cheerfulness with which she suffered the torments of the illness afflicting her.

§ 121
Improvement that occurred through obedience to the Mother General.

Ad 110: What is said about the Servant of God's obedience in this her last illness, I attest, as well as the fact of her rising from bed to receive Communion in the Chapel, and the subsequent improvement that came about through obedience to the Mother General, which was such that it caused wonder and consolation throughout the whole Community. I recall that Fr. Briuccia wished to come himself to say Mass and give her Holy Communion, and he lingered in holy conversation, after Mass, with everyone, our dear patient being present. And I also recall that Msgr. Briuccia himself, so great was the esteem in which he held the Servant of God, wished to show his inward consolation by having refreshments brought for all the Sisters present.

§ 122
Feelings of affection and gratitude towards the Sisters until the end.

Ad 111: These feelings of gratitude and affection towards the Sisters who attended her, in that worsening of the illness which afterwards showed itself, I attest and confirm.

§ 123
Spontaneously asked for the Holy Viaticum.

Ad 112: I was not present at the Holy Viaticum which the Servant of God asked for and received, but I afterwards heard related the great devotion and fervour with which she received the last Sacraments.

Ad 113: I was present at this testimony of obedience and devotion of all the Sisters, while the Servant of God was almost at the point of death. Being too weak to give them her blessing, she asked the Father Confessor to impart it to them in her stead.

Ad 114: I recall this telegram from the Mother General, which arrived after the Servant of God had already breathed her last.

§ 124
Great crowds to venerate the Servant of God's remains.

Ad 115: Indeed many people, of every condition, flocked to our House to venerate the Servant of God's mortal remains after her death. The Prince of Fitalia and the Princess his wife wished, at their own expense, to have the Servant of God's body photographed. I further attest that, also at the expense of the Prince and Princess of Fitalia, the Servant of God's body was buried three days after her death.

§ 125
The newspapers published public eulogies.

Ad 116: Of the eulogies the public newspapers made in our City, it is a well-known fact, and it is also known to me.

Ad 117: It is quite true what is said about the solemn funeral held at the central house for the Servant of God.

§ 126
Great attendance at the Servant of God's funeral.

Ad 118: I also attest and confirm what is said here about the presence of many people, especially the ladies of Palermo, at that solemn funeral, and about the beautiful funeral oration delivered by the late Fr. Gaetano Gabriele.

§ 127
Identification of the Servant of God's body in the presence of the Diocesan Vicar General, the Mother General, and many personalities.

Ad 119: The Servant of God died on 7 June 1885. About two years after her death, at the request of many prominent persons, Cardinal Celesia granted that the Servant of God's body be placed in a place of deposit. The Mother General then came to Palermo specially to attend that ceremony. Indeed, in the presence of Msgr. Cirino, then Vicar General of the Archdiocese, and of the entire Curia staff, of our Mother General, and of many distinguished personages, both ecclesiastical and lay, the Servant of God's body was exhumed and placed in a place of deposit.

§ 128
Devotion of those who attended the exhumation.

Ad 120: I attest that it is true that the opening of the coffin aroused devotion in those present, and that all there vied with one another, some to touch the body, others to obtain some object of the Servant of God's.

§ 129
Request for relics and information.

Ad 121: Everything said to have occurred on that occasion of the identification of the Servant of God's body is true, as is the record that was drawn up of it, and the Mass celebrated by Fr. Palazzotto.

§ 130
Universal desire to see her canonised.

Ad 122: This eagerness to want relics and to obtain news of the Servant of God is also known to me. And this on account of the Servant of God's beautiful virtues.

Ad 123: Most true, this universal desire to see the Servant of God raised to the honours of the altars.

§ 131
Graces and miracles obtained through the Servant of God.

Ad 124: I know of graces and miracles obtained through the Servant of God's intercession.

Ad 125: It happened, as the Article says, to me personally, the obtaining of the free passages for us to go to Naples, from Commendator Florio.

§ 132
Miraculous cures.

Ad 126: Sister Anna Battista Cusmano herself related to me the fact of her miraculous cure.

Ad 127: I heard Sister Anna Cunegonda Bonini herself relate the fact of her cure, which took place at the hospital of St. Xavier in Palermo.

§ 133
Many people go to the Servant of God's tomb to pray for graces.

Ad 129: Of the devotion Fr. Gagliani had towards Mother Sister Anna del Salvatore, it is something everyone knows, and it is also known to me. Just as I know of many people who commended themselves to the Servant of God to obtain special graces. On occasions of particular need, our Sisters, four or more of them, are accustomed to go on pilgrimage to ask for special graces, and it is not rare for them to obtain them. And I also know that even lay persons go to her tomb for this purpose of obtaining graces.

Ad 130: What is said in this Article, and which concerns my own person, I attest and swear to. I found myself in the town of Terranova, in Sicily, on the occasion of the second journey I made, as Provincial, through the houses of Sicily. Traveling by carriage from Caltanissetta to Terranova, with other Sisters, on reaching a certain point the horses took fright. It was a moment of great terror. I jumped from the rear of the carriage and pulled the Sisters after me. At that moment I noticed nothing; but the next day I began to feel pains. I had to leave again, but just as I was about to get into the carriage, I felt such pains that I could not bear them. A hernia had formed, because of the jump I had made, which tormented me horribly. During the night I felt I was dying. The doctor had said that the next day I would inevitably have to be operated on. He said: either the operation or death. But I turned to our Sister Anna del Salvatore, begging her to grant me some relief from my dreadful pains. I applied to my stomach the photograph and the veil of the Servant of God. At a certain moment I felt, in the afflicted spot, something like the loosening of a knot. I grew calm, the pains ceased, and I immediately felt cured. I called the Sisters to rejoice with me, so that I was able to continue my journey. The next day, the doctors having come, they marveled at my recovery and did not know what to attribute it to, if not a miracle. Asked whether I had anything further to add, I answered: "I have obtained from the Servant of God special graces in the exercise of my office as Provincial of this Province of Sicily, and not only this, but also personal graces, both in the moral and the material order."

§ 134
Witness's cure after applying a relic of the Servant of God.

WITNESS III
Fr. ENRICO FILITI

Procedural scope: From Session XIV of 30 July 1907 (Proc. p. 190) to Session XVI of 24 August 1907 (Proc. p. 205).

Name, surname, date and place of birth: Enrico Filiti, born in 1846 in Palermo.

State and profession: Priest, canon of the Cathedral, Private Chamberlain of His Holiness.

Quality of the witness: Eyewitness.

Witness's age when he met the Servant of God: 34 years.

Servant of God's age when the witness met her: 38 years.

Witness's age at the time of testimony: 61 years.

Duration of acquaintance and its origin: The witness met the Servant of God when the Daughters of Saint Anne, newly arrived in Palermo, made a pilgrimage to the Shrine of Montepellegrino; later, appointed confessor of the community, he also confessed the Servant of God until her death.

Observations on the witness, the scope, and the content of the testimony: The witness concisely sets out the singular virtues of the Servant of God, which he could observe directly thanks to close contact for about five years, attending her in her pious agony and death.

§ 135
General information about the witness.

Ad 2 interr., proc. pag. 191, testis respondit:

My name is Enrico Filiti, I am 61 years old, born in Palermo, residing at Corso Pisani, 197, son of the late Giuseppe and of Carmela Marino. I am a Canon of this Cathedral and a Private Chamberlain of His Holiness.

§ 136
Scope of knowledge.
§ 137
The Servant of God was a woman of "spirit".

Ad 7: I first met the Servant of God, Sister Anna of the Most Holy Saviour Orsi, on the occasion of a pilgrimage the Daughters of Saint Anne made to the Shrine of Montepellegrino, having been invited by Msgr. Zuccaro, who was then their General Director and Protector in Palermo. There I learned that the Servant of God was a woman of spirit, and so she was presented to me, and so everyone considered her.

Ad 8: I have always considered the Servant of God a holy woman; and it would be a true consolation for me to see her honoured with the honours of the Altars.

Ad 14: I met the Servant of God when she came to Palermo as Superior, sent by the Superior General of the Daughters of Saint Anne.

§ 138
Was most exact in observing all her duties and esteemed by the Sisters.

I therefore declare that everything I shall say about the Servant of God I learned in the external forum. § 139
Had most living faith.
§ 140
Love for God.
§ 141
Love for her fellow Sisters and the poor.

Ad 17: The view held of the Servant of God, as a woman adorned with every kind of virtue, was widespread not only in the Community but also among all who knew her. Her most living faith showed itself in every action and word of hers. Of her ardent love for God everyone spoke, and I myself often sensed it. The Sisters told me that she spent whole nights behind the altar of the Blessed Sacrament, in adoration, in their private Chapel. She always aspired to the eternal possession of her beloved God, which was the sole goal of every one of her actions. Her Charity towards the Sisters was immense; she helped them, sympathised with them, encouraged them to sacrifice. She loved to attend to the sick, especially the poorest. Her Prudence showed itself in directing the Community, so that all lived in unbroken peace. Christian Justice was for her like a special virtue, giving to God what was God's and to the neighbour what was the neighbour's. Temperance then made up her whole life: being most mortified, eating only the bare necessary, when she even managed that.

§ 142
Prudence and justice.
§ 143
Temperance.
§ 144
Fortitude.
§ 145
A model of humility.

Her Fortitude seemed almost a paradox in her, for one could not explain how so modest and humble a person could harbour a heart unfailingly strong and resistant to all the difficulties that stood in the way of the exercise of her virtues and of her office as Superior.

§ 146
Poverty and Chastity.
§ 147
Obedience.

She was truly humble: and I know with what disparaging words she spoke of herself, and how she strove to hide her virtues, which, however much she tried [sic], were eminent and revealed themselves on their own... Poverty she truly professed: dressing plainly, seeking no distinction of any kind. Chastity shone in her through the modesty of her conduct and her quite reserved way of dealing with people.

As for her Obedience to Superiors, I assume it, since she did nothing that was not in keeping with the holy Rule and the orders of her Superiors.

§ 148
Practiced the virtues to a heroic degree.

Ad 18: By heroic virtue I understand that which surpasses the ordinary, even that usually observed in pious persons. Now, as far as I could observe and sense, the virtues practiced by the Servant of God far surpassed the ordinary.

§ 149
Received the last Sacraments with faith and fervour.

Ad 22: As the Servant of God's Confessor, I was present at her last illness and death. She received the last Sacraments with faith and fervour and seemed to long to be united with her divine Spouse. I recall that she called the Sisters around her bed and urged them to observe the Institute's Rule. Among them, many, moved by affection and reverence for the Servant of God, had come from various places on the Island, as if to pay homage to her holiness.

§ 150
Many people asked for relics.

Ad 23-24: Many people flocked to the Chapel of the Sisters' House to venerate the body laid out there. Among these people were some of high social standing. And all vied with one another to obtain some relic of the Servant of God, especially the Sisters.

The Servant of God's body was buried in the Daughters of St. Anne's own family tomb in the Cemetery of St. Ursula; it was later exhumed with the intervention of the Curia and placed in a place of deposit in the same Cemetery of St. Ursula.

§ 151
The body was exhumed and placed in a place of deposit.

Ad 26: Of the Servant of God's virtues people spoke, and still speak, among the Sisters Daughters of St. Anne; of other outside persons I do not know.

§ 152
The fame of her virtues endures after death.

Ad 27: I can attest that all those who knew her held the opinion that the Servant of God was holy.

Ad 28: I do not know of anything having been written against the Servant of God, either in life or after death.

Obedience.

Humility.

§ 166
General information about the witness.

My name is Maria Teresa Patti di Sorrentino, I am 46 years old, born in Palermo and residing at Via D'Ossuna, 88; daughter of the late Francesco and of Laura Longo e Settimo; I am a religious Daughter of St. Anne and Superior of the St. Anne educational Institute.

§ 167
Scope of knowledge and devotion to the Servant of God.

Ad 7: On the occasion of attending to a housekeeper of mine, I met Sister Anna del Salvatore Orsi, which happened shortly after the arrival of the Daughters of St. Anne in Palermo.

§ 168
Holy resignation and peace amid trials.

§ 169
Her conduct was always edifying.

Ad 16: I knew the Servant of God closely, and I can assure that I never had anything to note about her conduct, either as a Christian or as a religious: the Servant of God's conduct was for me a continual edification.

§ 170
Was perfect in every virtue.

Ad 17: I affirm right away that the Servant of God was most perfect in every kind of virtue: however, I reserve the right to answer specifically for each virtue when the Articles are addressed.

§ 171
The Servant of God's virtues were extraordinary.

Ad 18: I answer as above, in general, that the virtues the Servant of God practiced were of an extraordinary degree, above the ordinary run of good Christians and religious. This I was able to note from the frequent conversations I had with the Servant of God.

§ 172
True and sincere humility in every act and word.

Ad 19: Nothing proud or vain did I observe in her during the time I knew her; on the contrary, the truest and most sincere humility showed itself in her every act and word.

§ 173
Had extraordinary gifts.

Ad 20: It is necessary here for me to state beforehand that I did not embrace the religious state of the Daughters of St. Anne until several years after the Servant of God's death: therefore, on certain things, I can only answer from having heard them said. On this point, I answer that from various Sisters I heard of extraordinary gifts, ecstasies, and other similar things.

§ 174
The witness cured of a serious illness through the Servant of God's prayers.

Ad 21: Even back when I was still a lay person, I had a very good relationship with the Servant of God: now, finding myself seriously ill, not to say gravely so, my friend, today a religious of St. Anne under the name Serafina Gregory, full of faith, went of her own accord to Sister Anna del Salvatore so that she would pray for my recovery. She, on hearing that my condition was so serious, exclaimed: "Poor creature, better it be me, O Lord, than her. Yes, we shall pray, we shall pray." The fact is that that night I felt better, and the next day I was cured, so much so that the doctor had to confess that this improvement was something extraordinary, and that he took back what he had said the day before, that my condition was seriously grave.

§ 175
The Servant of God's serenity during her last illness.

Ad 22: The Servant of God died on 7 June 1885 of infectious puerperal fever. I went to visit her every day, and I could observe her calm and resignation; indeed she showed herself glad to die.

Ad 23: I can say nothing of what happened at her death, as she died in the evening around ten o'clock; nor did I see her again after her death. I learned, however, that the body was laid out in the Sisters' chapel and that many people went to see her.

§ 176
At her exhumation, everyone asked for some relic.

Ad 24: I was present at the exhumation of the Servant of God's body to be placed in a place of Sacred Deposit. The Sisters go to the tomb to pray and ask for special graces.

§ 178
Reputation for holiness in life.

Love for God.

Begged alms with humility and grace.

and instilled it in the Sisters.

The Servant of God was most humble.

On her death.

Attentive to the Sisters even at the extremity of her life.

§ 215
Cure of Sister Teresa Macaluso.

Ad 130: This fact was told to me by the Provincial herself when she returned from Terranova. And I add a prodigious fact that happened to Sister Teresa Macaluso, Superior and foundress of the Institute of the Sacred Hearts in Palermo. She had a sarcoma on her neck which the doctors judged absolutely incurable and which could not be operated on at all. Meanwhile, the good Sister Macaluso effectively commended herself to the Servant of God, applying to the spot an object belonging to her. The fact was that after a few days the sarcoma disappeared entirely. This fact astonished those close to her, such as Cavaliere Landolina, my sister the Princess of Torrebuona, and others, and even the very doctor Cataliotti who had treated her and declared her incurable. He was so amazed at the fact that, going down the stairs, he kept exclaiming: "A miracle, a miracle." Doctor Cataliotti drew up a certificate on it, declaring that such a cure was not at all within the bounds of science. § 216
General information about the witness.

My name is Giuseppe Palazzotto, I am 67 years old, born in Palermo, living at via Volturno no. 97, son of the late Emmanuele and Angela Martinez. I am master Chaplain of the Cathedral of Palermo.

Ad 6: I have come only to testify on behalf of the Servant of God Sister Anna Salvatore Orsi, for the glory of God.

§ 217
Scope of knowledge and the witness's esteem for the Servant of God.

Ad 7: I knew the Servant of God from her first arrival in Palermo, having been one of those who went to receive the Daughters of St. Anne when they came to this City. She always showed herself most grateful, and I showed her all the esteem she deserved, having known even then that she was truly a servant of God. § 218
The Servant of God was a perfect Christian and an excellent religious.

Ad 8: I have always had veneration for the Servant of God and wish her to be exalted with the honours of the Altars.

§ 219
Was adorned with every virtue.

Ad 16: As regards the Servant of God's life while she was in Palermo, I can assure that I could observe in her a perfect Christian and an excellent religious, and the Sisters spoke of her to me in the same way.

§ 220
Faith shone in her.

Ad 17: Having frequented the House of the Daughters of St. Anne from their first arrival in Palermo, I can attest that the Servant of God Sister Anna del Salvatore Orsi was adorned with every kind of virtue.

§ 221
Placed all her trust in God.

In particular, I can say that a great faith in God shone in her, and the Sisters told me that the Servant of God spent whole nights before the Blessed Sacrament, seated on the Altar step.

§ 222
Ardent charity.

As for Hope, I heard from her own lips with what ardent desires she longed for Heaven, and how, in every circumstance, she placed all her trust in God alone.

Charity, then, was ardent in her, she being always afire with Divine Love: she always spoke like a Seraph.

§ 223
Was all things to all, sparing herself nothing.

As for Charity towards the neighbour, I can say and attest that she was all things to all, sparing herself nothing, both towards the Sisters, to whom she behaved as a true mother, and in attending the sick at home, hastening with great love to carry out this pious office. As for the other virtues, not being able to specify in particular what she did, I reserve the right to answer in the Articles.

§ 224
Her virtues were extraordinary.

Ad 18: By heroic virtue I understand that which surpasses the ordinary and the common. Now, that these virtues of hers were extraordinary is evident from the way she practiced them. I can attest for my part that the Servant of God, in fulfilling her duties even when gravely ill, strove so hard that it was astonishing simply to see her carrying out certain most burdensome tasks.

§ 225
Humility.

Ad 19: She never said anything at all that redounded to her own praise, nor, as far as I know, did she write anything of that kind.

Ad 20: On this Interrogatory, nothing is known to me personally; but the Sisters related to me many things as extraordinary in the Servant of God, which I never believed to be beyond belief.

§ 226
Resignation and joy in suffering.

§ 227
A great crowd at the funeral; everyone asked for relics of the Servant of God.

§ 228
The Servant of God's remains placed in a place of sacred deposit.

Reputation for holiness in life.

Ad 26: Indeed [sic] even while the Servant of God was alive, the opinion of her holiness was general.

§ 230
Reputation for holiness after death.

Ad 28: I never heard a word against the Servant of God's holiness.

Ad 30: I can add or take away nothing further for now; reserving, however, the right to say something more when I testify on the Articles.

§ 231
In Palermo, she won everyone's esteem.

Ad 15, proc. p. 240: I knew the Servant of God when she came to Palermo, first as Superior and then as Provincial, and I can say that she quickly won everyone's esteem here.

§ 232
Faith.

Ad 21: I confirm this Article, for the time the Servant of God was in Palermo.

§ 233
Was an apostle.

WITNESS VI
Sister ANNA SERAFINA GREGORY

Procedural scope: From Session XXIII of 26 October 1907 (Proc. p. 253) to Session XXIV of 19 November 1907 (Proc. p. 259).

Name, surname, date and place of birth: Sister Anna Serafina Gregory, in the world Francesca, born in 1856 in Rome.

State and profession: Religious Daughter of Saint Anne.

Quality of the witness: Eyewitness.

Witness's age when she met the Servant of God: about 24 years.

Servant of God's age when the witness met her: about 38 years.

Witness's age at the time of testimony: 51 years.

Duration of acquaintance and its origin: The witness had not yet entered the Institute of the Daughters of Saint Anne when she met the Servant of God in Palermo; she kept company with her, together with Maria Teresa Patti di Sorrentino, until her death.

Observations on the witness, the scope, and the content of the testimony: The witness shows good knowledge of the Servant of God, and in her detailed testimony she highlights all the virtues practiced, in an uncommon way, by the Servant of God, underscoring in particular her charity towards God and neighbour, her deep and sincere humility, and her spirit of prayer.

§ 250
General information about the witness.

Ad 2 interr., proc. pag. 254, testis respondit:

My name is Sister Anna Serafina Gregory, in the world Francesca, I am 51 years old and was born in Rome, I live in the Institute of St. Anne in Palermo, I am the daughter of the late Count Girolamo and Baroness Luisa Ancajanui: I am a religious in the Institute of the Daughters of St. Anne.

Ad 6: No one coached me on the answers to give.

§ 251
Scope of knowledge.

Ad 7: With the Servant of God Sister Anna del Salvatore Orsi being in Palermo, I had occasion to draw near to the said Servant of God, in the company of Signora Maria Teresa Patti di Sorrentino, both of us being then lay persons.

§ 252
Trust was placed in the Servant of God's prayers.
§ 253
Was most mortified.
§ 254
Died with joy.

Ad 17: As for the theological virtues, I can say that great faith was placed in her prayers, and what we asked of her was obtained. I too heard it said how the Servant of God even spent whole nights before the Blessed Sacrament. How she was most mortified, to the point of having no bed at all. It is also known to me that, having visited her gravely ill in her last illness, we found her seated in an armchair, and she only took to bed on the last day. On this occasion I heard from her own lips these words, which she spoke with the greatest rapture of soul: "What a beautiful day, what a beautiful day this is for me!"

§ 255
Governed with great prudence and charity.

I also heard it said that the Servant of God governed the Community with great prudence and charity, so much so that all the Sisters esteemed her and considered her a Saint.

§ 256
Love of God drove her to serve her neighbour.

As for charity towards her neighbour, she was a flame of charity, and that love for God burning in her breast drove her towards the suffering neighbour: and so she hastened, ready and cheerful, to attend to the sick, who, it was said, always wanted her; for it was said that when she came, they suffered less.

§ 257
Full of love for God and deeply humble.
§ 258
Had the gift of prayer.

Ad 18: By heroic virtue I understand a virtue that is above the common, the ordinary. Now, when I drew near the Servant of God, I saw how, in her expressions and her actions, she truly blazed with love of God like a Seraph. I saw in her a deep humility; she placed herself beneath everyone's feet. And this I saw and judged to be true and never affected: as sincere as the way the Saints speak and act. This was the esteem that I and others held for the Servant of God.

§ 259
Foretold to the witness that she would become a religious.

Ad 20: On this Interrogatory I can say that she had the gift of prayer, to the point of obtaining what she asked of God.

As to the gift of prophecy, I can say, from what happened to me, that I often tried to probe her to learn my future, and she told me that I would become a Daughter of St. Anne. I confess, however, that at the time I had no thought at all of embracing that Institute, also because I saw the austere life the Servant of God led.

§ 260
Was seen in ecstasy, lifted off the ground.

As for ecstasies and other such things, I myself never saw any, but I heard it told by a certain Sister, namely Sister Anna Amante La Barbera, who, invited by the Servant of God, while still a laywoman, spent the night together with her in the religious House, and saw her rise from the ground, caught up in the heavenly love flooding her heart. And it was after this wondrous event that the good Sister La Barbera embraced the Institute, in which she still perseveres today.

§ 261
Was glad to die: she longed to be united with the Lord.
§ 262
Burial in the Cemetery of St. Ursula and identification of the body.

Ad 22: I do not recall the exact day of the Servant of God's death; but I can attest that, having gone with Sister Anna Teresa Patti to visit the Servant of God on her deathbed, we found her greatly suffering but cheerful and glad to die, longing to be united with the Lord. I recall that, a few hours before the Servant of God died, we left, as the Princess of Fitalia was then arriving. I believe she received the Holy Sacraments in the morning.

Ad 24: On this Interrogatory, I can say that the Servant of God was buried in the Cemetery of St. Ursula, and that after some time she was placed in a place of deposit. I was not present when the identification of the Servant of God's body took place.

§ 263
People regarded her as a saint.

Ad 26: I have already said that the Sisters of the Institute and all the other people who came near her regarded the Servant of God as a Saint.

§ 264

§ 265

Ad 27: This reputation for holiness of the Servant of God also grew after her death; and I know that many commended themselves to her intercession, and still today hold her in much devotion and trust: the late Mother Foundress too nourished this devotion and trust. Indeed she often commended herself to her, particularly in certain very grave circumstances. And it was she who wished the Cause of Beatification of the Servant of God to be promoted.

§ 266
Prodigious cure of Teresa Macaluso.

Ad 29: On this Interrogatory, I attest having heard that many graces, and perhaps miracles, were obtained from God through the Servant of God's intercession. I recall having heard that Sister Teresa Macaluso, Foundress of the Institute of the Sacred Heart in Palermo, was cured of a sarcoma on her neck by the mere application of the Servant of God's portrait to the afflicted spot. I do not know the circumstances of the fact.

WITNESS I
Sister ANNA MARGHERITA TRIPI

Procedural scope: Session II of 21 December 1995 (Proc. p. 270)

Name, surname, date and place of birth: Sister Anna Margherita Tripi, in the world Provvidenza, born in Termini Imerese on 1 September 1911.

State and profession: Religious Daughter of Saint Anne, formerly a missionary in Argentina; currently retired.

Quality of the witness: De auditu (by hearsay).

Observations on the witness and on the content of the testimony: The witness summarises biographical information about the Servant of God and is convinced of her reputation for holiness, which she observed among her fellow Sisters both in Argentina and in Sicily; she also relates a grace received by a friend through the Servant of God's intercession.

Ad 2 interr., proc. pag. 270, testis respondit:

§ 284
General information about the witness.

My name is Sister A. Margherita Tripi (at baptism, Provvidenza), daughter of the late Loreto and Genoveffa Cottone, born in Termini Imerese on 1.09.1911, residing in Palermo, Corso Calatafimi 833, in the Institute of the Daughters of St. Anne. I have been a professed religious among the Daughters of St. Anne since 1929. I was a missionary in Argentina for about 25 years and now I am in our House of rest and prayer.

Ad 3: 1) I am bound to the Servant of God because I belong to the same religious Congregation she belonged to, and because I hold her in veneration.

2) I am moved to give my testimony to contribute to the favourable outcome of this Cause.

3) I have received no instructions or suggestions regarding my testimony.

§ 285
Sources of her knowledge about the Servant of God.

Ad 4: My knowledge and information about the Servant of God comes from biographical notes published in some pamphlets, including the one written by Sister A. Frati Roberta.

§ 286
The Servant of God's writings.

Ad 5: I know that some writings of the Servant of God exist, but I have not read them nor do I know where they are.

Ad 6: I know that, with the Archiepiscopal Curia of Palermo, there are the Acts of the Process begun about a century ago.

Ad 7: 1) I learned that the Servant of God, from girlhood, lived in poverty, devoting herself to family tasks since she had been orphaned of her father. Later she followed her religious vocation, entering the Congregation of the "Daughters of St. Anne" founded by Mother Rosa Gattorno.

§ 287
Bore trials and difficulties with patience and resignation.

In that Institute, unfortunately, she suffered slander and various humiliations, which she knew how to bear with patience and resignation to God's will. By the Foundress she was sent to Palermo to direct the Sicilian Province of the Congregation. I know that in Palermo she was esteemed by the ecclesiastical authorities, above all for her dedication to the service of the poor.

§ 288
Esteem for the Servant of God.

2) From all I have said, I have formed the conviction that the Servant of God was truly heroic in the exercise of the virtues and, particularly, in her submission to her Superiors, as well as in her great humility and her generous dedication to the service of the poor.

§ 289
Was greatly esteemed and called the "Little Saint of Palermo".

3) It is known to me that the particular and principal activity carried out by the Servant of God was that of her provincial superiorship in Sicily, which she took on with great responsibility and which was appreciated by superiors and the faithful, so much so that she, the Servant of God, came to be called the "Little Saint of Palermo".

§ 290
Her distinguishing mark: generous charity towards the poor.

4) It seems to me that the distinguishing mark of the Servant of God's spirituality is to be found in her generous charity towards the poor. And, in this respect, she could be a model for contemporary society.

§ 291
The witness's devotion to the Servant of God.

5) I have devotion to the Servant of God, because she was an exemplary Sister; besides commending myself to her in my prayers, I strive to imitate her in my spiritual and religious life.

§ 292
Her reputation for holiness kept growing.

6) I have already said that the Servant of God's reputation for holiness arose even while she was alive; indeed - I repeat - she was called the "Little Saint of Palermo". This reputation was maintained while the Servant of God lay buried in the Cemetery of St. Ursula, in a single ground-level tomb, where the faithful went to ask for spiritual and temporal favours. When, afterwards, the Servant of God's remains were exhumed and placed in our chapel, in the same cemetery, the influx of the faithful - as I learned - diminished somewhat; but it has resumed and today keeps increasing, after the re-exhumation of the remains that took place about 35 years ago, a ceremony at which I was present.

§ 293
News of the Cause of Beatification, in Argentina.
§ 294
Uninterrupted reputation for holiness in the Sicilian houses.

7) Since I was a missionary in Argentina, I had no way of knowing whether the Servant of God's reputation for holiness circulated in our Congregation there. I can only say that in Argentina the Sisters knew that a Cause for the Servant of God's Beatification had been opened in Palermo, but they did not know its progress or outcome. When afterwards I was in Palermo, and particularly after the second exhumation of her remains, I learned that her reputation for holiness had always circulated in our Sicilian Houses. I recall that at that time we had about seventy of our religious Houses in Sicily.

8) I am not aware of any writings or rumours from people and Sisters contrary to the Servant of God's reputation for holiness or to this Cause of Beatification.

§ 295
The Servant of God's current burial place.

Ad 8: 1) The Servant of God is currently buried in the family chapel of our religious Institute, situated in the Cemetery of "St. Ursula".

2) It is known to me that the current tomb is frequently visited by the faithful who show their devotion to the Servant of God and implore graces through her intercession.

§ 296
No improper cult is paid to her.

3) Neither at the Servant of God's tomb nor elsewhere - as far as I am aware - has any improper public cult been paid to the Servant of God.

Only the holy cards published by the Postulation circulate.

4) From a friend of mine, Maria Terranova, I learned that she obtained the following grace through the Servant of God's intercession.

§ 297
Cure attributed to the Servant of God.

The said Terranova, in fact, was to undergo a surgical operation, as a result of the findings on the X-rays; but when everything was ready for the operation, the doctors noticed that the ailment shown by the X-rays had by then disappeared, and so they did not consider the operation necessary. I shall take care, if I can, to learn more particulars about the grace I have related, and possibly to produce precise certifications.
